You will experience the themes of automating, accelerating, and enhancing a biomedical research process where time is critical. You will learn how to implement a highly transferrable, multi-industry OCI solution pattern. In this LiveLab, you will train your own image classification model on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) using OCI AI Vision. You will experience the themes of automating, accelerating, and enhancing a biomedical research process where time is critical. You will learn how to implement a highly transferrable, multi-industry OCI solution pattern. The LiveLab is divided into two Labs: loading and labeling a provided dataset, followed by model training and serving.

An image classification model will be able to tell you what your image represents, based on all of the shapes and colors present in the image. This experiment will require our image classifier to serve as a cell classifier. As a cell classifier, your machine learning model will be able to discern images of cells from non-cells in the provided dataset, where the images were captured using a technique called coherent diffraction imaging.

The concept of the cell classification story and the dataset used in this LiveLab has been provided by Dr. Xin-hua Hu, from his machine learning experiment in the Physics department at East Carolina University. The cell classifier is a practical option for medical professionals during their research process, who would traditionally distinguish images of cells from non-cells by their own visual observation, and record their findings manually.

With large datasets, this process can be incredibly time-consuming and impractical. However, by offloading this important busywork to the cell classifier, and focus on tasks where their broad and deep range of knowledge and skills can be much more economically applied - and derive their analyses much faster where time is of the essence.

This solution pattern will be especially interesting if you can identify processes in your business and industry where automated and accurate visual analysis will render valuable time and cost savings. 1 1412 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. You will learn how to implement a highly transferrable, multi-industry OCI solution pattern. The LiveLab is divided into two Labs: loading and labeling a provided dataset, followed by model training and serving.

An image classification model will be able to tell you what your image represents, based on all of the shapes and colors present in the image. This experiment will require our image classifier to serve as a cell classifier. As a cell classifier, your machine learning model will be able to discern images of cells from non-cells in the provided dataset, where the images were captured using a technique called coherent diffraction imaging.

The concept of the cell classification story and the dataset used in this LiveLab has been provided by Dr. Xin-hua Hu, from his machine learning experiment in the Physics department at East Carolina University. The cell classifier is a practical option for medical professionals during their research process, who would traditionally distinguish images of cells from non-cells by their own visual observation, and record their findings manually.

With large datasets, this process can be incredibly time-consuming and impractical. However, by offloading this important busywork to the cell classifier, and focus on tasks where their broad and deep range of knowledge and skills can be much more economically applied - and derive their analyses much faster where time is of the essence.

This solution pattern will be especially interesting if you can identify processes in your business and industry where automated and accurate visual analysis will render valuable time and cost savings.

The proliferation of cloud computing has brought heightened concerns about industry-standard regulations especially around protecting data and its privacy. Today, most organizations want to know where their data is stored, and who has access to it. This creates a key concern about managing data residency—the requirement that data be stored in a specific geographic location.
Data sovereignty generally refers to how data is governed by regulations specific to the region in which it originated. These types of 
regulations can specify where data is stored, how it is accessed, how it is processed, and the life-cycle of the data.


In this Livelabs, learn how Oracle Sharding meets data sovereignty requirements and supports applications that require low latency and high availability.
1. Sharding makes it possible to locate different parts of the data in different countries or regions – thus satisfying regulatory requirements where data has to be located in a certain jurisdiction.

2. It also supports storing particular data closer to its consumers. Oracle Sharding automates the entire lifecycle of a sharded database – deployment, schema creation, data-dependent routing with superior run-time performance, elastic scaling, and life-cycle management.

3. It also provides the advantages of an enterprise RDBMS, including relational schema, SQL, and other programmatic interfaces, support for complex data types, online schema changes, multi-core scalability, advanced security, compression, high-availability, ACID properties, consistent reads, developer agility with XMLTYPE, JSON, and much more. 207 300 153 259 207 300 662 297 1722 252 3669 259 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Database - Globally Distributed Database, Database - Oracle AI Database, Database - Oracle Partitioning Application Dev., Business Analyst, DBA, DevOps Engineer, IT Administrator, Technology Manager

SQL Empowerment in Oracle Database 26ai: Leveraging Domains and Features 11427 3835 Database hope.fisher@oracle.com Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Complete database Mapped From Current Wms 3835 11427 Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Complete Database 12/8/2025 7/20/2023 Individual author Individual .5 11 10 11 54 database Mapped From Current Wms github_pages Live GitHub workshop path (high confidence) high Workshop-specific Git evidence 2026-04-03 2026-04-03 2026-04-03 2023-04-07 2026-04-03 2025-03-19 change github.io refs to cdn (#1011) klazarz 23aifree/workshops/sandbox-sql-domains 23aifree/workshops/sandbox-sql-domains/manifest.json 2023-10-01 Kaylien Phan, William Masdon Hope Fisher, Program Manager David Start 23aifree/change-pw/change-pw-sql.md Acknowledgement date trails latest Git update by 535 days WMS workshop update N/A Confirmed From Current Or Stable Id History Publish Type is present in the reconciled WMS record. 3835 11427 Workshop Published Private Quarterly QA Complete Database 12/8/2025 7/20/2023 Individual author Individual .5 https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=3835 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/database/23aifree/workshops/sandbox-sql-domains/index.html hope.fisher@oracle.com DB Product Management Power up with SQL domains in the Oracle Database 26ai - create and use single column and built-in domains, and validate JSON. Then take an in-depth look at features you should know - GROUP BY aliases, optional FROM clause, SQL Boolean, IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL clause, new table VALUE constructor, multi-value INSERTs, UPDATEs with RETURNING or with joins, and annotations. The use case domain functionality is a very powerful new "tool" for application development in Oracle Database 26ai. In general,  use case domains allow users to declare the intended usage for columns with a separate data dictionary objects so that abstract domain specific knowledge can be easily reused. You can use them to provide additional information to a stored column and you can define and validate data with them. Not only relational columns can be validated but also JSON data with the new VALIDATE clause. Like other database objects it can be created, dropped and altered. With it you have the freedom to change the validation logic or information without changing the table definition. 

A use case domain (short domain) is a dictionary object that belongs to a schema and encapsulates a set of optional properties and constraints for common values. Domains provide constraints, display, ordering and annotations attributes. After you define a domain, you can define table columns to be associated with that domain, thereby explicitly applying the domain's optional properties and constraints to those columns. So domains are used to provide additional information to a stored column (JSON or relational), and therefore, used to define and validate data.

You can create, alter and drop a domain in your own schema. To work with domains, you require the privilege CREATE DOMAIN.

There are 3 different types of domains: single column, multi column and flexible domains. In addition there are also built-in domains that you may use.

Overall, we present the following 10 Oracle Database 26ai features: 
- Aliases in GROUP BY clause
- FROM clause - now optional
- Boolean for SQL
- IF [NOT] EXISTS DDL clause
- New table VALUE constructor 
- Multi-value INSERTs
- RETURNING clause of UPDATE and MERGE statement
- Joins in UPDATE and DELETE
- Schema annotations, the new metadata for database objects
- Use case domains https://youtu.be/ksVgnhbxj9w 11 1006 10 972 11 1006 54 969 available_shared_title_scope shared_title_across_wms_records Dashboard metrics are title-level and shared by 2 current WMS records; they are not LiveLabs-ID-specific. Build a movie app with machine learning-powered recommendations with MySQL HeatWave and Oracle APEX

Welcome to this workshop in which you’ll follow step-by-step instructions to build the MovieHub application powered by MySQL HeatWave. MovieHub is a fictitious movie streaming application that delivers personalized recommendations using machine learning. It leverages the built-in HeatWave AutoML recommender system to predict, for example, movies that a user will like, or to which users a given movie should be promoted. You’ll build this app using the most popular low-code development platform, Oracle APEX, which will also enable you to create analytics dashboards in the application. You’ll develop a few scenarios both from the user's and the administrator's perspective.

This workshop walks you through the steps to get started using Oracle Access Governance to understand use cases such as access controls implementation, user access reviews, and enterprise-wide visibility for systems managed using Access Governance. 

Oracle Access Governance is a cloud-native identity governance and administration (IGA) service that provides enterprise-wide visibility to govern access to cloud and on-premises environments. With an intuitive user experience, dynamic access control, and a prescriptive analytics–driven access review process, it helps customers automate access provisioning, get insights into access permission and cloud infrastructure policy reviews, identify anomalies, and remediate security risks. Oracle Access Governance allows:
    Administrator to perform various system, service, and access control administrative tasks
    Campaign administrator to run intelligent access review campaigns for access governance and compliance
    Cloud Access Reviewers to review policy access insights and take informed decisions based on prescriptive analytics
    Users and user managers to validate access assigned to self and their direct reports, respectively.
    Access Control Administrator to automate access through Access Bundles, Roles, Identity Collections, Policies, and Approval Workflows.
    Users to request access provisioned various target systems

This lab walks you through the steps to get started using Oracle Access Governance with several use cases - access controls, access reviews, and enterprise-wide access browsing. In this workshop, a fictitious corporation is using Oracle Access Governance to manage and govern the application access of its employees and contractors. This lab shows how the database is connected to AG as a target system and implement access control by creating identity collections, approval workflows, roles, access bundles, and centralized policies. It also shows how to perform access review campaigns, and associated review tasks. https://cdnapisec.kaltura.com/p/2171811/embedPlaykitJs/uiconf_id/54927872?iframeembed=true&entry_id=1_mngovqor&config%5Bprovider%5D=%7B%22widgetId%22%3A%221_9h69sgh6%22%7D&config%5Bplayback%5D=%7B%22startTime%22%3A0%7D 1 1169 20 1094 110 1049 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. This workshop demonstrates how to use parsed data from your Legacy application for software modernization, like identifying Bounded Context or adding runtime data to identify Business Processes. The workshop is based on extracted data from a real-world sample and uses Oracle Graph Studio to analyze and visualize the data. 

Extracting the dependency data out of a data model, the SQL statements, the PL/SQL implementation, and the UI design and finally enhancing all of them with the user behavior of a legacy application is one of the key components of the Product PITSS.CON. It is used, e.g., to Modernize an Oracle Forms Application to APEX. The Graph Data model and various algorithms are integrated into PITSS.CON

The workshop focuses on the capabilities of the Oracle graph engine.

Explore how the new JSON Relational Duality Views (JRDVs) in Oracle Database 23ai make it simpler than ever for your DevOps teams to build robust applications at extreme speed without having to worry about how data is stored within your database. Author: Jim Czuprynski, Oracle ACE Director, Zero Defect Computing, Inc.

NoSQL databases have proliferated in recent years because they often use JSON documents as their basis for data storage and retention. But the advantages of JSON – simple datatype mapping, schema-less development, easy-to-understand hierarchies, and best of all, no curmudgeonly DBAs to deal with! – often neglect the myriad advantages of relational databases, including guaranteed data consistency, dramatically efficient queries, and high availability and recoverability in case of system failures.

With Oracle Database 23ai Free Developer Release and the power of Oracle REST Data Service, you can utilize the advantages of relational and document data storage in the same database. JSON Relational Duality is a landmark capability in Oracle Database 23ai that provides game-changing flexibility and simplicity for Oracle Database developers. This breakthrough innovation overcomes the historical challenges that developers have faced when building applications, either when using the relational model or when using the document model.

JSON Relational Duality helps to converge benefits of both document and relational worlds. Developers now get the flexibility and data access benefits of the JSON document model, plus the storage efficiency and power of the relational model. The new feature that enables this convergence is called JSON Relational Duality View.

Interacting with your Oracle Database with HTTPS and REST APIs can be as simple as picking the objects in your database you want to start working with.

Oracle REST Data Service (ORDS) includes a feature known as ‘AutoREST,’ where one or more objects are enabled, and REST API endpoints are automatically published. For example, a TABLE can be enabled for GET, PUT, POST, DELETE operations to get one or more rows, insert or update rows, delete rows, or even batchload multiple rows in a single request. This feature has been enhanced for 23ai to include similar REST access for JSON-Relational duality views. not_in_dashboard_snapshot unavailable No exact title row exists in the 28 September 2026 dashboard workbook. Enable REST calls with one command on your JSON Relational Duality Views with AutoREST. With Oracle Database 23ai Free Developer Release and the power of Oracle REST Data Service, you can utilize the advantages of relational and document data storage in the same database.

JSON Relational Duality is a landmark capability in Oracle Database 23ai that provides game-changing flexibility and simplicity for Oracle Database developers. This breakthrough innovation overcomes the historical challenges that developers have faced when building applications, either when using the relational model or when using the document model.

JSON Relational Duality helps to converge benefits of both document and relational worlds. Developers now get the flexibility and data access benefits of the JSON document model, plus the storage efficiency and power of the relational model. The new feature that enables this convergence is called JSON Relational Duality View.

Interacting with your Oracle Database with HTTPS and REST APIs can be as simple as picking the objects in your database you want to start working with.

Oracle REST Data Service (ORDS) includes a feature known as ‘AutoREST,’ where one or more objects are enabled, and REST API endpoints are automatically published. For example, a TABLE can be enabled for GET, PUT, POST, DELETE operations to get one or more rows, insert or update rows, delete rows, or even batchload multiple rows in a single request. This feature has been enhanced for 23ai to include similar REST access for JSON-Relational duality views.

In this workshop, you will use the Oracle Integration Rapid Adapter Builder - Visual Studio Code extension to build an adapter for the ACME Order Management application's REST APIs.

This workshop describes how to use the Oracle Integration Rapid Adapter Builder framework to develop a custom adapter which exposes REST APIs. You will :

•  Understand the role and benefits of the Rapid Adapter Builder in simplifying custom adapter development for Oracle Integration Cloud 
•  Set up prerequisites like having an Oracle Integration Cloud instance, installing required software (Visual Studio Code, Postman), and creating an IDCS client application 
•  Initialize a new workspace directory for adapter development using the Rapid Adapter Builder VS Code extension 
•  Configure the extension's publisher profile with Oracle Integration Cloud instance details and IDCS client credentials 
•  Import a Postman collection containing the APIs of the target application (e.g. ACME Order Management) and test the API calls 
•  Learn about the structure and sections of an Adapter Definition Document (ADD) that defines an adapter's metadata 
•  Generate an initial ADD automatically from the imported Postman collection using the extension 
•  Explore the generated ADD file and understand how to update sections like info, schemas, connection, actions, triggers, etc. 
•  Customize the ADD by modifying the adapter's name, description, request/response schemas, configurable connection properties, actions, triggers, etc. 
•  Validate the finalized ADD to ensure it is free of errors before publishing 
•  Publish and register the custom adapter bundle to the configured Oracle Integration Cloud instance 
•  Verify the successful deployment of the published adapter in the Oracle Integration Cloud instance 
•  Understand the workflow for incrementally updating an existing custom adapter definition

Oracle Integration 3 - Automate Invoice Processing with OCI Document Understanding 11664 3979 OIC - Integration kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Beginner oic Mapped From Current Wms 3979 11664 Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete OIC - Integration 9/10/2025 7/31/2025 Individual author Individual 2.75 198 109 198 694 1200 2516 Beginner oic Mapped From Current Wms github_pages Live GitHub workshop path (high confidence) high Workshop-specific Git evidence 2026-04-03 2026-04-03 2026-04-03 2022-09-07 2026-04-03 2024-07-22 change github.io refs to cdn (#110) klazarz opa-for-fusionApps/invoice-handling-process/workshops/tenancy opa-for-fusionApps/invoice-handling-process/workshops/tenancy/manifest.json 2024-06-01 Kishore Katta, Oracle Integration Product Management Kishore Katta Harris Qureshi (App Integration Specialist), Stanislav Tanev (OPA Product Management) opa-for-fusionApps/invoice-handling-process/introduction/introduction.md Acknowledgement date trails latest Git update by 51 days WMS workshop update N/A Confirmed From Current Or Stable Id History Publish Type is present in the reconciled WMS record. 3979 11664 Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete OIC - Integration 9/10/2025 7/31/2025 Individual author Individual 2.75 https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=3979 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/oic/opa-for-fusionApps/invoice-handling-process/workshops/tenancy kishore.x.katta@oracle.com Other Product Management In this Live Lab, we'll explore leveraging the OCI AI Services feature in OPA to build an automated invoice processing Orchestration workflow. This workflow will read invoice PDF documents, extract relevant data using AI powered document understanding service, validate the extracted information, and store it in a database. The workflow will notify the user if the extracted data is not approved. This tutorial will cover the following steps:

1. Ingesting Invoice PDF Documents: We'll start by ingesting invoice PDF documents into the workflow. This will be done by the stakeholder uploading the document by launching a processing application web form.

2. Extracting Invoice Data with OCI Document AI Service: Next, the workflow leverages OCI's Document AI Service to extract key information from the invoice PDFs, such as invoice number, date, total amount, line items, and vendor details. This AI Services document control leverages advanced machine learning models to understand the structure and layout of documents, enabling accurate data extraction.

3. Validating Extracted Invoice Data: After extracting the invoice data, we'll implement a validation process to ensure the integrity and completeness of the extracted information. This could involve checking for missing or inconsistent data

4. Triggering OIC Integration flow for saving the Invoices: If the extracted invoice data is deemed valid during the validation process, we'll trigger an OIC Integration flow. This Integration flow will initiate a series of actions to save the invoice in the database. We will OIC Event system to publish the Invoice details.

5. Storing Valid Invoice Data in a Database: A subscriber Integration flow will transform and persist the invoice details in a database for further processing or integration with other systems, such as accounting or enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems. For this Live lab we will consider the invoice records to be stored in a database. However, the design pattern can easily be extended to create another seamless subscriber integration flow and create an invoice record in ERP cloud.

Throughout the Live Lab, we'll explore the usage of OCI AI services- Document Understanding form control and extend the use case to invoke an integration flow to persist the invoice record in DB. We will also explore OPA Analytics to identify the process trends, and errors, and understand how long processes take to complete and why.

By the end of this Live Lab, you'll have a comprehensive understanding of how to build an end-to-end invoice processing Integration using OCI AI Services, ensuring accurate data extraction, validation, and storage, while streamlining the processing of valid invoices through automated workflows. 198 304 109 307 198 304 694 289 1200 316 2516 334 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Application Integration - Integration, Process Automation AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Application Integration - Integration, Process Automation Database Cloud Service - Autonomous AI Transaction Processing, Database Cloud Service - OCI Document Understanding, Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) - OCI Integration Business Analyst, Business User, Developer, Low Code Developer AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Application Integration - Integration, Business Analyst, Business User, Database Cloud Service - Autonomous AI Transaction Processing, Database Cloud Service - OCI Document Understanding, Developer, Low Code Developer, Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) - OCI Integration, Process Automation

A full set of OCI security tools and securely configured OCI resources will be created as the foundation for a production cloud. This lab walks through the process of deploying the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Core Landing Zone (previously named ‘OCI CIS Landing Zone’). This is a curated Terraform-based template to automate provisioning of a secure OCI tenancy and all required services that is compliant with the Center of Internet Security (CIS) benchmark for OCI. Landing Zones help customers accelerates onboarding to OCI and achieve a strong, secure architecture foundation and best-practice configurations for future scaling.

This lab provides an overview of the OCI Core Landing Zone and its components, an explanation of how to deploy the landing zone via GitHub or OCI Resource Manager service, how to use it to assess the security posture of your OCI environment, and how to maintain it and ensure ongoing CIS compliance.

In the lab, users will create a set of CIS-compliant cloud resources to jumpstart their development on OCI. In our lab, we tackle optimising data retrieval within a controlled environment, using the NYC taxi dataset as a test bed to showcase OCI Redis's effectiveness as a caching layer. Our setup features a Flask application querying this dataset from an Oracle Autonomous Database, focusing on specific date ranges for trip data.
We integrate OCI Redis Cache to manage frequently accessed data, streamlining the process: on a data request, the app first checks  OCI Redis Cache, significantly reducing response times if cached. This approach not only demonstrates efficient data flow between cache and database but also emphasises the role of caching in minimising database load and enhancing query performance.

This workshop outlines a two-step approach to tackle a problem by leveraging two different models. The first model generates descriptions for images, while the second model creates vectors for these textual descriptions. The second model is loaded in the database allowing for both vector generation and AI Vector Search without leaving the database. By separating the tasks, the complexity is reduced, making it easier to use existing models, as very few can handle both images and text simultaneously. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is an important component in Generative AI.  Here are three reasons why RAG should be included in your Gen AI application.
1.	LLMs can hallucinate or generate incorrect responses to your prompt if it has not been trained to respond to the query in the prompt.  Retraining LLMs to produce the responses you want can be very expensive.
2.	Businesses and enterprises have lots of private and confidential information and they want to leverage the power of Gen AI with LLMs with the least cost.  
3.	Businesses and enterprises have streaming data and need LLM responses to this data in near real time.

And that’s where RAG comes in.  RAG allows important context to be included with the prompt to the LLM.  In this workshop you will provide context and store that information in the form of vectors in Oracle Database 23ai, and use the Oracle AI Vector Search capability to return the context to augment LLM responses. AI tools are changing modern healthcare. In this workshop we show how Oracle AI is helping identify  cancer by using the Oracle Database, OCI, and AI Services and popular full-stack languages and frameworks including Flutter, Java (SpringBoot), JavaScript (React, Express, Node), Python, Rust, etc.

Authors: Paul Parkinson, Nicholas Cusato, and Divit Gupta

ML and AI tools are unprecedentedly changing Modern Healthcare. Given the speed of innovation and global outreach, it can be challenging for patients and healthcare providers to stay abreast of the latest technological advances and how they will impact the future.

In this LiveLabs AI for Healthcare, Learn about the latest innovations in Healthcare, Detect Breast Cancer using OCI Vision at an early stage. Detect Cardiovascular disease with Electrocardiogram (ECG) Reports and OCI Anomaly Detection. Use the power of OCI Document Understanding to submit medical expenses, or using OCI Speech, ask a doctor about specific medical symptoms and get a response from a virtual Doctor (not a replacement for actual medical advise of course) leveraging the power of Oracle Gen AI. Chat with a virtual doctor through Oracle Digital Assistant, asking questions related to Breast cancer or Lung cancer or Covid and how to diagnose them. Analyze complex clinical data or genome sequences with Oracle Analytics Cloud or locate the nearest Hospital with Oracle Spatial and Maps and contact them. And much more.

All this, when running on top of the world's most powerful database, Oracle Autonomous Database and popular full-stack languages and frameworks including Flutter, Java (SpringBoot), JavaScript (React, Express, Node), Python, Rust, etc.

This workshop is designed to equip participants with a comprehensive understanding of common pitfalls associated with handling credentials in OCI environments. By delving into real-world scenarios and practical examples, attendees gain valuable insights into the potential risks and vulnerabilities that can arise from mishandling credentials.

The workshop kicks off with a cautionary tale, illustrating a scenario where a user inadvertently stores credentials in a public bucket. This all-too-common mistake serves as a powerful reminder of the potential consequences when security measures are not diligently followed. Participants are guided through the anatomy of such a lapse, exploring how an unauthorized person could exploit the exposed credentials to gain unauthorized access and compromise the security of the entire system.

As the workshop progresses, emphasis is placed on the importance of adopting a robust credential management strategy. The focal point of this strategy is the usage of OCI Vault, a versatile and secure solution for managing secrets and protecting sensitive data in dynamic cloud environments. Attendees will be taken through a step-by-step demonstration of how OCI Vault can be seamlessly integrated into cloud workflows to enhance security and mitigate the risk of unauthorized access.


In this workshop, you will:

Lab 1
- Understand the challenges associated with storing credentials in OCI buckets for automation purposes.
- Recognize the potential risks and security implications of mishandling credentials within an OCI setup.
- Experience the consequences of unauthorized access resulting from the misuse of credentials.

Lab 2
- Comprehend the risks associated with publicly accessible buckets in OCI.
- Explore the perspective of an attacker gaining unauthorized access to a public bucket.
- Analyze the potential exploits and risks involved when managing credentials in publicly accessible storage.

Lab 3
- Learn the importance of secure credential management in OCI.
- Utilize OCI Vault to securely store and manage credentials.
- Understand the proper workflow of accessing credentials from OCI Vault and applying them to interact with REST APIs. 76 462 59 420 76 462 187 519 340 558 1261 491 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Development, Development - Cloud Native, Development - Security Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Development, Development - Cloud Native, Development - Security Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - OCI Identity and Access Application Dev., DevOps Engineer, Developer, IT Administrator

With microservice based architectures, each microservice typically uses its own database.  When a request spans multiple microservices, there’s a good chance it will run into a problem where two or more updates must succeed, or none do. Like if I send you money from my bank, but your account isn’t updated for some reason. Unfortunately, in the microservices world, local database transactions can’t span microservices. So how do you overcome the dual write problem?  
 
With Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices, or MicroTx you don’t have to worry about making sure all updates happen. It’s a workflow engine to ensure data consistency across microservices.   
 
It takes on the burden of error handling and recovery so that the microservices and developers can focus on business logic and not on underlying technical issues. It keeps microservices consistent with each other, reducing complexity.

In this workshop, you will learn how to use MicroTx to maintain data consistency across multiple ORDS applications by deploying and running a Bank Transfer application. The Bank Transfer application is created in PL/SQL and deployed using ORDS in Oracle Database. MicroTx provides a transaction coordination microservice to maintain consistency in the state of various databases participating in a transaction. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4j74C4GobzY 1736 119 482 132 1736 119 2468 134 2499 194 2500 336 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Application Dev., Database - ORDS, Database - Oracle AI Database, Database - Oracle APEX, Developer, Developer - Low Code, Development, Development - Cloud Native, Development - Database, IT, Low Code Developer, Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices - MicroTx, Technology Manager Development, Development - Cloud Native, Development - Database Development, Development - Cloud Native, Development - Database Database - ORDS, Database - Oracle AI Database, Database - Oracle APEX, Developer - Low Code, Oracle Transaction Manager for Microservices - MicroTx Application Dev., Developer, IT, Low Code Developer, Technology Manager

Improve application performance with True Cache 11454 3933 Database - MAA sambit.p.panda@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Intermediate database Mapped From Current Wms 3933 11454 Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Database - MAA 9/21/2026 8/17/2023 Individual author Individual 342 157 342 1131 2465 5456 Intermediate database Mapped From Current Wms github_pages Local Git mirror workshop path (high confidence) high Workshop-specific Git evidence 2025-09-11 2025-09-11 2025-09-11 2022-05-31 2025-09-24 WMS ID-11454: Fixing some more typos (#873) sambitppanda truecache/workshops/dbw25-tenancy truecache/workshops/dbw25-tenancy/manifest.json 2025-08-01 Sambit Panda, Consulting Member of Technical Staff , Vivek Vishwanathan Software Developer, Oracle Database Product Management Sambit Panda, Consulting Member of Technical Staff Pankaj Chandiramani, Shefali Bhargava, Jyoti Verma, Ilam Siva truecache/introduction/introduction.md Acknowledgement date trails latest Git update by 54 days WMS workshop update N/A Confirmed From Current Or Stable Id History Publish Type is present in the reconciled WMS record. 3933 11454 Workshop Published Public Quarterly QA Complete Database - MAA 9/21/2026 8/17/2023 Individual author Individual https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=3933 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/database/truecache/workshops/dbw25-sandbox/index.html sambit.p.panda@oracle.com DB Product Management - PTS Many large scale Web applications faces performance issues when a a database becomes the bottleneck.

Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use True Cache to improve scalability by offloading queries and reducing the number of requests and connections to the primary database. Why use True Cache?
True Cache can be used to scale a read-mostly application even without partitioning data. When primary database becomes the bottleneck , True Cache can be used to offload the primary and scale the workload. Also the data is always consistent and recent within a single query, this is important when there are joins across multiple rows.


This usage model of true cache through the JDBC requires minimal application change to use the functionality. Applications connect to only one service. Application uses setReadOnly(true) and setReadOnly(false) calls to mark some sections of code as "read only". If True Cache instances are configured, the JDBC driver will internally maintain, for each logical connection, 2 physical connections, one to a primary instance and one to an True Cache instance. The JDBC driver automatically sends SQL statements in "read-only" blocks to the True Cache instance.

What's in the workshop
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a Primary database configured with True Cache. The demo application is a Java program using the 23c JDBC driver. Its simulates a high number of transactions for the primary database and how off loading the read only queries to true cache helps in application performance.

It demonstrates:

How to set up True Cache.
Schema creation and initial data load to the primary database
The demo application shows the transactions running against the primary database and how switching to true cache helps in performance improvement . 342 253 157 256 342 253 1131 215 2465 198 5456 192 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Development - Database Development - Database Database - Oracle AI Database Application Dev., DBA

With Oracle Database 23ai Free Developer Release and the power of Oracle REST Data Service, you can utilize the advantages of relational and document data storage in the same database. JSON Relational Duality is a landmark capability in Oracle Database 23ai that provides game-changing flexibility and simplicity for Oracle Database developers. This breakthrough innovation overcomes the historical challenges that developers have faced when building applications, either when using the relational model or when using the document model.

JSON Relational Duality helps to converge benefits of both document and relational worlds. Developers now get the flexibility and data access benefits of the JSON document model, plus the storage efficiency and power of the relational model. The new feature that enables this convergence is called JSON Relational Duality View.

Interacting with your Oracle Database with HTTPS and REST APIs can be as simple as picking the objects in your database you want to start working with.

For example, a TABLE can be enabled for GET, PUT, POST, DELETE operations to get one or more rows, insert or update rows, delete rows, or even batchload multiple rows in a single request. Leverage OCI and open frameworks to improve productivity and efficiency of your applications. In this lab, you will explore the power of OCI Generative AI and its potential to revolutionize your applications. Through hands-on exercises, you'll learn how to integrate Generative AI into your solutions to tackle real-world business challenges, such as document summarization, natural language conversations grounded in documents, content generation for websites, video transcriptions, and more.

We'll begin with an overview of the services and frameworks utilized in this lab, followed by a series of practical exercises. These exercises will guide you through setting up your environment, building and testing a Gen AI chat application, interacting with PDF documents, comparing files, summarizing content, and more. By the end of this lab, you'll have the skills to leverage OCI Generative AI to enhance the productivity and efficiency of your applications.

Agenda:

Introduction
Get an overview of the lab objectives and the impact of Generative AI on modern applications.

Demo of Applications
Preview the applications you'll be building during the lab.

Review of Services and Frameworks
Explore the OCI services and open frameworks that you'll use to implement AI-driven solutions.

Lab 1: Setting Up and Testing the Environment
Prepare your environment and ensure that all necessary tools and services are correctly configured.

Lab 2: Gen AI Chat App
Build a chat application powered by Generative AI, enabling natural language interactions.

Lab 3: Chat With PDF Documents
Implement a feature allowing users to chat and extract information from PDF documents.

Lab 4: Compare PDF Files
Learn how to compare and contrast content across multiple PDF files using Generative AI.

Lab 5: Document Summarization
Automatically generate concise summaries of documents to save time and enhance productivity.

Lab 6: Chat and Summarize Web Pages
Extend your application's capabilities to interact with and summarize web pages.

Lab 7: Chat and Summarize YouTube Videos
Integrate AI to transcribe and summarize content from YouTube videos, making information more accessible.

Outcome:

Using OCI PostgreSQL, OCI Generative AI, OCI Document Understanding, OCI Speech, OCI Vision, and custom binary parser. In today’s modern business world, people want access to information fast, but when it comes to document scans, it can be difficult to access the text from those documents. In this lab, we’ll walk you through automating this process. - Transfer Excel files from an FTP server to OCI Object Storage using OIC native actions.

This comprehensive hands-on workshop will equip you with the skills to automate and streamline data workflows by integrating Oracle Integration (OIC) with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) services. In modern businesses, efficient data handling is critical, and this workshop addresses that need by walking you through the creation of a real-world integration scenario where data in Excel files is transferred, processed, and transformed automatically.

During this workshop, you will learn to build an end-to-end integration flow that automates file handling from an FTP server, converts files to a new format, and prepares them for further processing. Whether you work in data integration, IT operations, or business process automation, this workshop will give you the practical experience needed to implement solutions that save time and reduce manual effort.

Key Learning Objectives:
Transfer Excel Files to OCI Object Storage: You will learn how to use OIC native actions to list, download, and transfer Excel files from an FTP server to OCI Object Storage for secure and temporary storage.

Invoke Serverless Functions to Convert Excel Files: You will deploy an OCI serverless function that converts Excel files (.xls/.xlsx) into CSV format, automating data transformation.

Process CSV Files in OIC: After converting the files, you will use OIC to read and stage CSV files, preparing them for further integration tasks like reporting, analytics, or updating business applications.

What You Will Learn:
How to integrate OIC with OCI services to automate file transfers and transformations, creating scalable workflows.
Practical use of OIC native actions to manage Object Storage and invoke serverless functions.
Best practices for data security and processing, ensuring that file handling is efficient, secure, and streamlined.
Hands-on experience with real-life business cases, enabling you to apply these skills in your organization’s data operations. 212 298 161 250 212 298 878 255 1569 268 3184 290 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Application Integration - Integration, Development, Development - Cloud Native Application Integration - Integration, Development, Development - Cloud Native Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) - OCI Integration Developer, Low Code Developer

This hands-on workshop will equip you with the knowledge and skills to modernize your legacy Oracle Forms applications using Oracle APEX. Whether new to APEX or looking to refine your skills, this workshop will provide valuable insights and practical experience. Welcome to our Oracle Forms to Oracle APEX Transition Workshop! This hands-on workshop will equip you with the knowledge and skills to modernize your legacy Oracle Forms applications using Oracle APEX. Whether new to APEX or looking to refine your skills, this workshop will provide valuable insights and practical experience. Throughout the workshop, you will learn to understand the fundamental differences and similarities between Oracle Forms and APEX and how to map components from one to the other.

You will also analyze and extract crucial business logic from your existing Oracle Forms applications, set up the necessary database infrastructure to support your APEX applications and use the Create Application Wizard to develop a web-based application. Learn how to integrate generative AI into the Oracle Digital Assistant by connecting it to a large language model, or LLM, hosted in OCI Gen AI Service. An LLM is an AI system that has been trained on vast amounts of text data. By integrating your ODA skill with an LLM, you enable it to not only field a range of user input, but also to respond with context-appropriate answers in a human-like tone. Oracle Digital Assistant (ODA) can be integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance its capabilities. OCI Gen AI Service offers LLMs trained on vast amounts of text data, enabling them to perform tasks like text summarization and sentiment analysis. By connecting ODA with OCI Gen AI, you can make it more versatile in handling user input and generate human-like responses.

Learn how to integrate generative AI into the Oracle Digital Assistant by connecting it to a large language model, or LLM, hosted in OCI Gen AI Service. An LLM is an AI system that has been trained on vast amounts of text data. These models can be trained on various domains to perform a variety of tasks, including audience-specific text summarization and sentiment analysis of chat histories.

By integrating your ODA skill with an LLM, you enable it to not only field a range of user input, but also to respond with context-appropriate answers in a human-like tone. To help the LLM predict the most likely words or phrases for its responses, you send it the appropriate context and instructions in a block of text known as a prompt. In response, the LLM generates a completion, a sequence of words or phrases that it believes are the most probable continuation of the prompt.

Running AI workloads on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE) is more straightforward than you might expect. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides a variety of GPU-enabled nodes, available in both virtual and bare metal options, designed to act as worker nodes within your Kubernetes clusters. These nodes come pre-configured with NVIDIA drivers and a device plugin daemon-set, making setup quick and easy.

Oracle DB 23ai adds significant value by offering robust vector storage capabilities, which are critical for managing complex, high-dimensional data such as embeddings used in AI applications. Utilizing Oracle DB 23ai as a vector store allows AI systems to efficiently store and retrieve data for more advanced operations. With OCI, you can securely run Large Language Models (LLMs) in your own environment, enabling them to draw insights from your enterprise’s specific data. Build AI agents using Python & LangChain, integrating with Oracle AI Database 26ai for relational & RAG data. Learn to create custom tools, design prompts, & leverage context memory for tasks like email automation & PDF creation. Perfect for developers & AI enthusiasts to master intelligent systems & streamline workflows. In recent months, the field of AI Agentics has gained significant traction, showcasing the remarkable potential of AI to perform advanced logical reasoning and execute complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. AI agents represent a transformative leap in artificial intelligence, enabling systems to not only process information but also make decisions, interact with diverse data sources, and integrate with external tools to achieve sophisticated outcomes. This workshop is designed to provide participants with a comprehensive, hands-on understanding of building AI agents, empowering them to harness these cutting-edge capabilities for real-world applications.
The session will guide attendees through the process of creating a fully functional AI agent using Python and the LangChain framework. Through a practical example, we will demonstrate how an AI agent can seamlessly interact with relational data and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) data stored in an Oracle AI Database 26ai. Additionally, participants will learn how to extend the agent's functionality by integrating external tools, such as sending emails or generating PDFs, showcasing the versatility of AI agents in automating diverse workflows.

Workshop Highlights:
Environment Setup and Dependencies: Learn how to configure the necessary development environment, including installing required libraries and tools to ensure a smooth agent-building process.

Creating Custom Tools: Discover how to design and implement custom tools that enable the AI agent to perform specialized tasks, such as interacting with APIs or processing specific data formats.

Designing Effective Prompt Templates: Master the art of crafting prompt templates that guide the AI agent’s behavior, ensuring accurate and contextually relevant responses.

Initializing and Running the Agent: Gain hands-on experience in setting up and deploying the AI agent, observing how it processes inputs and executes tasks in real time.

Leveraging Context Memory: Explore the role of context memory in enabling the agent to maintain continuity and make informed decisions based on prior interactions.

Throughout this workshop, we'll explore:

1. Setting up the environment and dependencies

DB Security - TDE key management with Oracle Key Vault
Migrate an encrypted Oracle database 19c to centralized key management with Oracle Key Vault.

In this hands-on lab, you’ll migrate an Oracle Database 19c encrypted with TDE from a local wallet to centralized key management with Oracle Key Vault (OKV). You’ll upload pre-migration TDE master keys to OKV, then remove them from the encrypting server to align with PCI DSS requirements. You’ll also use tagged keys to associate TDE master keys more easily with PDBs, reducing manual steps and configuration errors. By the end, you’ll have a repeatable workflow for centralizing database encryption keys with auditing and rotation readiness.

Data-level security defines what a user in an analytics application can access inside a report. When run by two different users, the same report can bring up different data. The structure of the view is the same for all users, unless a user does not have access to the subject area, in which case the report displays an error. Ensuring that only authorized people can access specific data is important to prevent sensitive information from being queried or run. records.searchable: Prevent and Detect Fraud with Immutable and Blockchain Tables on Oracle Autonomous Database 11831 4142 Database amit.ketkar@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed Beginner security Mapped From Current Wms 4142 11831 Workshop Published Public Completed Database 9/9/2025 4/23/2025 Individual author Individual 40 31 40 121 318 676 Beginner security Mapped From Current Wms github_pages Live GitHub workshop path (high confidence) high Workshop-specific Git evidence 2026-04-07 2026-04-07 2026-04-07 2025-03-21 2026-04-07 2025-04-25 change githubio refs to cdn (#407) klazarz blockchain-table-new/workshops/tenancy blockchain-table-new/workshops/tenancy/manifest.json 2025-04-01 Vinay Pandhariwal Amit Ketkar, Pavas Navaney, Vinay Pandhariwal blockchain-table-new/introduction/introduction.md Matches Git month WMS workshop update N/A Confirmed From Current Or Stable Id History Publish Type is present in the reconciled WMS record. 4142 11831 Workshop Published Public Completed Database 9/9/2025 4/23/2025 Individual author Individual https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=4142 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/security/blockchain-table-new/workshops/ amit.ketkar@oracle.com Other Learn how Oracle Blockchain Tables and Immutable Tables provide tamper-resistant data storage within your database. This LiveLab walks you through their key features, ensuring data remains secure, verifiable, and unchangeable. Oracle Blockchain Tables and Immutable Tables offer a structured approach to maintaining data integrity, security, and verifiability within the Oracle Database. This LiveLab demonstrates how these technologies use cryptographic signing, digest generation, and verification to preserve trust and support auditability. In Blockchain Tables, each row is cryptographically chained to the previous one, forming a secure and traceable record history. The session will guide attendees through the process of creating a fully functional AI agent using Python and the LangChain framework. Through a practical example, we will demonstrate how an AI agent can seamlessly interact with relational data and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) data stored in an Oracle AI Database 26ai. Additionally, participants will learn how to extend the agent's functionality by integrating external tools, such as sending emails or generating PDFs, showcasing the versatility of AI agents in automating diverse workflows.

Workshop Highlights:
Environment Setup and Dependencies: Learn how to configure the necessary development environment, including installing required libraries and tools to ensure a smooth agent-building process.

Creating Custom Tools: Discover how to design and implement custom tools that enable the AI agent to perform specialized tasks, such as interacting with APIs or processing specific data formats.

Designing Effective Prompt Templates: Master the art of crafting prompt templates that guide the AI agent’s behavior, ensuring accurate and contextually relevant responses.

Initializing and Running the Agent: Gain hands-on experience in setting up and deploying the AI agent, observing how it processes inputs and executes tasks in real time.

Leveraging Context Memory: Explore the role of context memory in enabling the agent to maintain continuity and make informed decisions based on prior interactions.

Throughout this workshop, we'll explore:

1. Setting up the environment and dependencies
2. Creating custom tools for our agent
3. Designing effective prompt templates
4. Initializing and running the agent

This comprehensive lab is designed to provide hands-on experience with migrating on-premises databases to Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB) on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). Participants will develop foundational knowledge of ADB architecture, its core capabilities, and the best practices for secure and efficient migrations. 

The lab begins by demonstrating how to establish secure and reliable connections to ADB, ensuring users are equipped to interact with the cloud database environment. Next, users will perform readiness checks on their existing environments, verifying all prerequisites—such as network connectivity, database and schema requirements, and necessary tools—are in place for a smooth migration.

The lab walks participants through Oracle’s Cloud Migration Analyzer, a utility that scans your source database and offers tailored recommendations on the optimal migration strategy. Users will also measure and evaluate network latency between their systems and ADB to verify adherence to Oracle’s best practices for a successful migration. 

For actual data movement, the lab provides step-by-step guidance on exporting source data using Oracle Data Pump and importing it into ADB, using NFS. In addition, participants will explore migrating data using the DB Link method for direct transfers, giving users practical experience with multiple migration paths. 

After performing data migration tasks, the lab concludes with exercises that teach users how to monitor ADB’s performance, utilize troubleshooting tools, and analyze workload metrics to ensure the migrated environment operates efficiently.

The lab begins by demonstrating how to establish secure and reliable connections to ADB, ensuring users are equipped to interact with the cloud database environment. Next, users will perform readiness checks on their existing environments, verifying all prerequisites—such as network connectivity, database and schema requirements, and necessary tools—are in place for a smooth migration.

The lab walks participants through Oracle’s Cloud Migration Analyzer, a utility that scans your source database and offers tailored recommendations on the optimal migration strategy. Users will also measure and evaluate network latency between their systems and ADB to verify adherence to Oracle’s best practices for a successful migration. 

For actual data movement, the lab provides step-by-step guidance on exporting source data using Oracle Data Pump and importing it into ADB, using NFS. In addition, participants will explore migrating data using the DB Link method for direct transfers, giving users practical experience with multiple migration paths. 

After performing data migration tasks, the lab concludes with exercises that teach users how to monitor ADB’s performance, utilize troubleshooting tools, and analyze workload metrics to ensure the migrated environment operates efficiently. 

Throughout the lab, users gain valuable skills in planning, executing, and validating ADB migrations, preparing them for real-world cloud adoption scenarios.

Learn to use Oracle Database GenDev AI to automatically generate data access APIs, database objects, and data privacy policies by breaking down an application into modules. We will use Oracle APEX AI Assistant to create UI on these APIs and also showcase how you can leverage MCP to connect with GenDev. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how artificial intelligence is transforming the way data-centric applications are built. We'll demonstrate how you can leverage Oracle Database GenDev AI to automatically and reliably generate robust data access APIs and database objects by modularizing your application design. Using a real-world scenario—a sample conference management system—you’ll see how application modules are decomposed and the corresponding APIs are created.

Next, we'll show how Oracle Application Express (APEX) AI Assistant can rapidly generate the user interface for your app, sitting seamlessly on top of the generated APIs. The workshop will dive deep into defining, iterating, and enforcing data privacy and role-based access control rules within the application.

Finally, you’ll discover how next-generation multi-modal clients, such as Claude Desktop, can interact with Oracle GenDev MCP Server. We'll demonstrate generating APIs and application code simply by describing your requirements using a large language model (LLM), making application development more accessible and efficient. This hands-on workshop is designed to help you get started with MySQL Enterprise Edition, a powerful database management system. You'll learn the fundamentals of installing, configuring, and using MySQL Enterprise Edition, with a focus on its JavaScript Stored Procedure and Function feature.

In this workshop, you'll work through a series of guided tasks and exercises that will help you understand the basics of MySQL Enterprise Edition, including:

Installing and configuring the server
Creating and managing databases
Using JavaScript to create stored procedures and functions
Implementing a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, and PHP) stack—or a LAMP stack with Python/Flask instead of Apache/PHP—for web development
Deploying a sample web application, the "Sakila Film Time Converter", which demonstrates the use of MySQL JavaScript functions

- Automated data extraction from PDF invoices without manual entry
- Smart approval routing based on business rules and risk factors
- Payment terms optimization for better cash flow management This comprehensive hands-on workshop will equip you with the skills to build intelligent document processing solutions by integrating Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Document Understanding services. In today's digital business environment, manual invoice processing represents a significant operational bottleneck, and this workshop addresses that challenge by walking you through the creation of a real-world enterprise automation scenario where invoice documents are automatically extracted, analyzed, and routed through intelligent business rules.

During this workshop, you will learn to build an end-to-end intelligent automation flow that combines artificial intelligence for document understanding with sophisticated business decision logic for approval routing and payment optimization. Whether you work in accounts payable, financial operations, business process automation, or enterprise integration, this workshop will provide you with the practical experience needed to implement solutions that dramatically reduce manual effort, improve accuracy, and accelerate business processes.

Key Learning Objectives

- Extract Structured Data from Unstructured Documents
- Implement Intelligent Business Decision Logic
- Orchestrate End-to-End Automated Flow
- Design Event-Driven Architecture for Scalability

What You Will Learn

- Advanced Document Intelligence Integration:

How to integrate OIC with OCI Document Understanding to automate invoice data extraction, creating scalable workflows that eliminate manual data entry while maintaining high accuracy and reliability. You'll master the configuration of document understanding models, data mapping techniques, and error handling strategies for production deployments.

- Sophisticated Business Rules Implementation:

Practical use of OIC Decisions components to implement complex business logic using the FEEL (Friendly Enough Expression Language), including multi-variable decision tables, contextual risk assessment, and hierarchical decision structures that mirror real-world business policies and approval processes.

- Enterprise Integration Architecture Patterns:

Best practices for cloud-native integration design, including event-driven architecture, business rules design patterns.

- Real-World Financial Business Automation:

Hands-on experience with practical business scenarios on how to implement business rules such as vendor risk assessment, approval routing optimization, payment terms calculation, and cash flow management, enabling you to apply these skills directly to your organization's financial operations and accounts payable processes. 135 355 46 474 135 355 439 355 1268 303 2585 328 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Application Integration - Integration, Development, Development - Cloud Native Application Integration - Integration, Development, Development - Cloud Native Database Cloud Service - OCI Document Understanding, Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) - OCI Integration Developer, Low Code Developer

This workshop walks you through the steps to get started using Oracle Access Governance to understand use cases such as access controls implementation, user access reviews, and enterprise-wide visibility for systems managed using Access Governance. 

Oracle Access Governance is a cloud-native identity governance and administration (IGA) service that provides enterprise-wide visibility to govern access to cloud and on-premises environments. With an intuitive user experience, dynamic access control, and a prescriptive analytics–driven access review process, it helps customers automate access provisioning, get insights into access permission and cloud infrastructure policy reviews, identify anomalies, and remediate security risks. Oracle Access Governance allows:
    Administrator to perform various system, service, and access control administrative tasks
    Campaign administrator to run intelligent access review campaigns for access governance and compliance
    Cloud Access Reviewers to review policy access insights and take informed decisions based on prescriptive analytics
    Users and user managers to validate access assigned to self and their direct reports, respectively.
    Access Control Administrator to automate access through Access Bundles, Roles, Identity Collections, Policies, and Approval Workflows.
    Users to request access provisioned various target systems

This LiveLab takes you through deploying OpenKruise, a CNCF project that extends Kubernetes workload management, on Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE). OpenKruise enhances the standard Kubernetes controllers by introducing powerful capabilities such as automated sidecar injection, seamless in-place updates, and more advanced StatefulSet behaviors for improved scalability and reliability.

Throughout the workshop, you will provision an OKE cluster using a pre-built automation repository, install OpenKruise, and then explore how it can be used to simplify and optimize application lifecycle management. You will experiment with real-world scenarios that demonstrate how sidecar containers can be automatically injected into workloads, how applications can be updated in place without requiring pod recreation, and how stateful applications can benefit from safer and more flexible update strategies. Finally, you will clean up all deployed resources to avoid unnecessary costs.

By the end of this lab, you will have practical, hands-on experience running OpenKruise in a production-grade Kubernetes environment on OKE and a deeper understanding of how it can streamline and strengthen workload deployments. 29 829 22 870 29 829 98 820 139 867 267 875 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Development, Other - Administration Development, Other - Administration Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - OCI OKE Application Dev., DevOps Engineer

Experience drop-in MongoDB compatibility with Oracle’s autonomous scaling, security, and performance—no code changes required. This lab demonstrates how to build a CRUD To-Do List application using Node.js, Express, and the official MongoDB driver. Instead of connecting to a traditional MongoDB backend, you’ll point the app to Oracle Autonomous JSON Database (AJD) using its MongoDB API endpoint.

You’ll see how Oracle AJD can act as a seamless, drop-in backend for MongoDB workloads—with no changes to drivers, APIs, or development workflow. The only change required is updating your connection string. The lab also highlights Oracle AJD’s built-in benefits, such as autonomous scaling, security, and high availability.

By the end of this lab, you’ll have a working web application that looks and feels like a classic MongoDB stack, but runs on Oracle Cloud. You'll configure GoldenGate to stream database changes as JSON payloads, then run an AI agent that consumes this stream, interprets the data in real-time, and responds to natural language queries. In this hands-on lab, you will build an intelligent AI agent that integrates with OCI GoldenGate Data Streams and leverages the power of JSON-relational duality views to deliver real-time insights and recommendations. The lab focuses on a practical, event-driven use case using live cart order data, where the AI agent performs semantic search across other orders to dynamically suggest items that a customer might want to add to their cart—enabling an intelligent, personalized shopping experience powered by streaming data.
As part of the lab, you will:
	•	Configure OCI GoldenGate to stream real-time transactional data as JSON payloads using Data Streams.
	•	Create and work with Oracle Database 23ai JSON-relational duality views to bridge structured and semi-structured data, enabling flexible access to both traditional relational schemas and modern JSON formats.
	•	Build an AI agent capable of understanding user queries in natural language and translating them into meaningful actions, such as recommending products or retrieving operational metrics.
	•	Implement real-time semantic search logic to analyze current cart contents and suggest complementary products based on patterns in past orders.
	•	Integrate a conversational interface that allows users to query GoldenGate operational metrics (e.g., lag, status, throughput) via chat, using natural language.
This lab demonstrates how you can combine Oracle's cutting-edge data streaming technology with AI to build context-aware, real-time, and highly responsive applications. Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use True Cache to improve scalability by offloading queries and reducing the number of requests and connections to the primary database. Why use True Cache?
True Cache can be used to scale a read-mostly application even without partitioning data. When primary database becomes the bottleneck , True Cache can be used to offload the primary and scale the workload. Also the data is always consistent and recent within a single query, this is important when there are joins across multiple rows.


This usage model of true cache through the JDBC requires minimal application change to use the functionality. Applications connect to only one service. Application uses setReadOnly(true) and setReadOnly(false) calls to mark some sections of code as "read only". If True Cache instances are configured, the JDBC driver will internally maintain, for each logical connection, 2 physical connections, one to a primary instance and one to an True Cache instance. The JDBC driver automatically sends SQL statements in "read-only" blocks to the True Cache instance.

What's in the workshop
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a Primary database configured with True Cache. The demo application is a Java program using the 23c JDBC driver. Its simulates a high number of transactions for the primary database and how off loading the read only queries to true cache helps in application performance.

It demonstrates:

This workshop is designed to help you quickly get started with developing applications using Oracle NoSQL Database. It shows the different methods by which your application can connect to the database and perform simple operations on it.
Oracle NoSQL Database offers various methods by which your application can access the database:
•	Using Integrated Development Environments (IDEs):
You can use integrated development environments to connect to the Oracle NoSQL database and develop your applications efficiently. Oracle NoSQL Database plugins are available for Microsoft Visual Studio Code and IntelliJ IDEs.

•	Using Software Development Kits (SDKs):
You can use the SDKs available in different programming languages to develop your applications. These SDKs enable applications to connect to the database using HTTP/HTTPS protocol via the Oracle NoSQL proxy.

•	Using SQL Command Line Interface (CLI):
You can use the SQL language in your applications to interact with the Oracle NoSQL Database.

In this workshop, you will be using  Microsoft Visual Studio Code to demonstrate the three methods. 
Also, you will be using a simplified version of the Oracle NoSQL Database called KVLite. KVLite provides a single storage node, single shard store, that is not replicated. 27 851 25 811 27 851 95 836 130 879 190 977 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Development - Database Development - Database Database - Oracle NoSQL DB Developer

Learn to create database-powered agents with persistent memory, semantic search, and enterprise data access using Oracle Select AI Agent framework. Hands-on with SQL. Most AI systems can answer questions. AI agents are built to do work.

In this hands-on workshop, you will build AI agents for a financial services company called Seer Equity. Their current systems cannot answer simple questions like loan status or pending applications. Instead of returning results, they explain how to look things up. That breaks trust and frustrates clients.

You will build AI agents that connect directly to a loan database and return real answers. When asked about a loan, the agent queries data and responds with the current status, amount, and owner. You will see exactly what the agent did and why it did it.

During the workshop, you will:

Build AI agents that act on data instead of explaining steps

Store and recall client information across interactions

Use prior decisions to guide new ones

Apply company policies stored in the database

Record every action for audit and compliance

You will use Oracle Database and the Select AI Agent framework to define tools, agents, tasks, and teams using SQL. By the end, you will have a working loan processing system built around AI agents that behave consistently and can be trusted.

No machine learning background required. This workshop demonstrates how to utilize Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI Agents to automate IT operations. A common and impactful use case has been selected for this demonstration—remediation of high CPU and memory utilization alarms. In this scenario, the OCI Generative AI Agent leverages a runbook retrieved via a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) tool to determine the appropriate remediation steps and trigger the necessary tools to resolve the issue.

While this workshop highlights a specific use case, the approach is extensible. Organizations can integrate OCI Generative AI Agents with existing IT Service Management (ITSM) systems to identify various IT operational issues and automatically execute relevant runbooks for resolution.

Key Components and Services Used:

OCI Autonomous Database (23ai) is utilized as the RAG database to store and retrieve operational runbooks.

OCI Email Delivery service is configured to send real-time notification emails to the IT operations team once remediation tasks are successfully completed.

OCI Monitoring is used to define and configure alarms for CPU and memory utilization, triggering alerts when usage exceeds 90%.

A test compute instance was provisioned to simulate CPU and memory stress using synthetic load generation tools (e.g., stress-ng), thereby creating realistic alarm scenarios.

OCI Agent Development Kit (ADK) was employed to develop and deploy the Generative AI agents.

Slack was integrated as the front-end interface, allowing IT users to query system health (e.g., CPU or memory alarms) and authorize the AI agent to perform remediation actions according to the runbook instructions.

This end-to-end setup showcases the potential of OCI Generative AI in streamlining IT operations, reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR), and enhancing operational efficiency through intelligent automation. 501 202 138 276 501 202 706 287 776 396 780 569 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) AI Services - AI Vector Search, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - Compute Instances, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - OCI Identity and Access, Database - Python DevOps Engineer, IT

Getting Started with AI Vector Search
This workshop will go through the basic steps of getting started with AI Vector search, including why AI Vector Search is so important and how to use AI Vector Search in applications.

This workshop will cover what AI Vector Search is and how it works. Included will be hands on exercises to:
- introduce similarity search
- add the new vector datatype
- verify ONNX embedding models
- create vector embeddings for text and images
- perform exact similarity searches
- create vector indexes and run approximate similarity searches
- combine similarity searches with normal relational queries
- use the data and queries defined in the lab to see how similarity search works in a pre-built APEX application
- learn how AI Vector Search can augment RAG queries and see a pre-built APEX chatbot works using AI Vector Search and RAG

This 15-minute hands-on lab demonstrates separation of duties by blocking even DBAs from accessing customer data unless explicitly authorized. This helps you meet regulatory compliance requirements with technical controls, not just trust. Imagine your Chief Compliance Officer walks in with urgent news: if DBA credentials are compromised, attackers get unrestricted access to all customer data. Regulations demand technical controls, not just trust. This 15-minute FastLab shows you how to implement separation of duties quickly and effectively with Oracle Database Vault. You'll experience a real-world compliance scenario on Oracle Autonomous AI Database. You'll start by demonstrating the problem: as a privileged administrator, you can query all sensitive customer data including names, emails, and phone numbers. Then you'll implement the solution using Database Vault realms. You'll create a mandatory realm that establishes a protected zone around sensitive schemas and objects. This technical control blocks all access attempts, even from DBAs and schema owners, unless users are explicitly authorized. You'll see firsthand how realm authorization works alongside standard database privileges to create layered security. By the end, you'll confidently demonstrate to stakeholders how Database Vault enables regulatory compliance while DBAs maintain their administrative capabilities, proving that your security model relies on technical enforcement, not trust alone 29 829 23 845 29 829 96 828 151 844 available_shared_title_scope shared_title_across_wms_records Dashboard metrics are title-level and shared by 2 current WMS records; they are not LiveLabs-ID-specific.
