In this workshop, you will learn how to deploy and manage NVIDIA NIM containers on Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE)  to run scalable, high-performance AI inference workloads. This session is designed for developers and MLOps engineers who want to operationalize NVIDIA AI models using Kubernetes-native workflows on OCI.

This workshop is ideal for developers, data scientists, and DevOps practitioners interested in:

- Deploying NIM on Kubernetes: Learn how to orchestrate and scale NVIDIA NIM containers using OKE for efficient AI inference in production.
- Harnessing NVIDIA GPUs for optimal performance: Experience how OKE integrates with NVIDIA GPU nodes to accelerate inference with TensorRT-optimized NIMs.
- Streamlining MLOps: Automate deployment, scaling, and lifecycle management of AI models using Helm, kubectl, and OCI DevOps tools within a unified cloud environment.

What you will learn
By the end of this workshop, you will have hands-on experience with:

- Creating an NVIDIA API Key and pulling NIM containers
- Setting up an OKE cluster with GPU-enabled nodes
- Deploying NVIDIA NIM using Helm or kubectl
- Exposing NIM services securely for inference
- Sending inference requests and monitoring performance with OCI tools 74 469 55 437 74 470 202 505 309 585 444 678 available_shared_title_scope shared_title_across_wms_records Dashboard metrics are title-level and shared by 2 current WMS records; they are not LiveLabs-ID-specific. 2 AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Development - Cloud Native AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Development - Cloud Native Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) - OCI OKE Data Scientist, DevOps Engineer

In this lab you will learn the basics of the Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench) by walking through a use case creating a medallion architecture. You will provision an AIDP Workbench and work with its components including catalogs, workspaces, compute clusters, notebooks, workflows, and RBAC. In this lab you will learn the basics of the Oracle AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench) by walking through a use case creating a medallion architecture using supplier data. You will provision an AI Data Platform Workbench (AIDP Workbench), create a catalog, and populate it with data. Then you will create a workspace and compute cluster. Using these you will process your data in the AIDP Workbench notebook interface. While processing the data you will create tables in your catalog to hold the bronze, silver, and gold levels of your medallion architecture. You will leverage models from the OCI Generative AI service to aid in transforming and enriching your data. Then you will create a series of workflows to run your data processing tasks on a schedule. Along the way you will learn about RBAC AIDP Workbench. Then you will connect OAC to your AIDP to visualize your gold tier data. Finally, you will connect your Fusion AI Data Platform (Fusion AIDP) instance to the AIDP Workbench so that you can bring your data assets from Fusion AIDP into AIDP Workbench for further use.

APEX-based agentic chatbot powered by APEX Workflow and multiple database-centric tools

This workshop brings you thru the development of a low-code agentic chatbot with multiple tools and with almost every part of the solution in the database. After provisioning the required resources, you create the APEX chat interface with a redwood design. From there you go thru the steps of developing three tools in the autonomous database. Each tool will be created in its own lab and called by the APEX chatbot. The tools will enable capabilities such as RAG, NL2SQL and the use of an external tool via an RDMS package. Finish off workshop by seeing how complex prompting can be answered with multiple tools.

Learn to create database-powered agents with persistent memory, semantic search, and enterprise data access using Oracle Select AI Agent framework. Hands-on with SQL. Most AI systems can answer questions. AI agents are built to do work.

In this hands-on workshop, you will build AI agents for a financial services company called Seer Equity. Their current systems cannot answer simple questions like loan status or pending applications. Instead of returning results, they explain how to look things up. That breaks trust and frustrates clients.

You will build AI agents that connect directly to a loan database and return real answers. When asked about a loan, the agent queries data and responds with the current status, amount, and owner. You will see exactly what the agent did and why it did it.

During the workshop, you will:

Build AI agents that act on data instead of explaining steps

Store and recall client information across interactions

Use prior decisions to guide new ones

Apply company policies stored in the database

Record every action for audit and compliance

You will use Oracle Database and the Select AI Agent framework to define tools, agents, tasks, and teams using SQL. By the end, you will have a working loan processing system built around AI agents that behave consistently and can be trusted.

No machine learning background required. This hands-on workshop walks you through setting up OCI services, configuring PostgreSQL, building Docker images, pushing them to OCI Container Registry, and automating your CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions for smooth, repeatable deployments. Learn how to build, containerize, and deploy a production-ready Spring Boot application using PostgreSQL on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). In this hands-on workshop, you will go step-by-step through the entire lifecycle of a modern cloud-native application—from code to deployment—using industry-best practices and fully automated pipelines.

You will start by setting up the required OCI services, including networking components, compartments, and access credentials. Then, you will provision and configure a managed PostgreSQL database and connect your Spring Boot application to it using secure environment variables. 

Building on this foundation, you will learn how to use GitHub Actions to automate every stage of your CI/CD pipeline. The workflow will check out your source code, install JDK 17, build your Spring Boot JAR, create and push a Docker image to OCIR, and finally deploy your application on OCI using OCI Container Instances. You will explore how the deployment process dynamically discovers the correct availability domain, generates the necessary JSON payloads for container, VNIC, and compute shape configurations, and launches a fully functional container instance with public network access.

By the end of the workshop, you will have a fully automated pipeline that builds, packages, stores, and deploys your Spring Boot application on Oracle Cloud—with each new push to the main branch triggering a fresh deployment. You will understand how your application connects to PostgreSQL through configurable environment variables, how container port mappings are defined, and how all components work together for smooth and repeatable cloud deployments.

This 15-minute hands-on lab demonstrates separation of duties by blocking even DBAs from accessing customer data unless explicitly authorized. This helps you meet regulatory compliance requirements with technical controls, not just trust. Imagine your Chief Compliance Officer walks in with urgent news: if DBA credentials are compromised, attackers get unrestricted access to all customer data. Regulations demand technical controls, not just trust. This 15-minute FastLab shows you how to implement separation of duties quickly and effectively with Oracle Database Vault. You'll experience a real-world compliance scenario on Oracle Autonomous AI Database. You'll start by demonstrating the problem: as a privileged administrator, you can query all sensitive customer data including names, emails, and phone numbers. Then you'll implement the solution using Database Vault realms. You'll create a mandatory realm that establishes a protected zone around sensitive schemas and objects. This technical control blocks all access attempts, even from DBAs and schema owners, unless users are explicitly authorized. You'll see firsthand how realm authorization works alongside standard database privileges to create layered security. By the end, you'll confidently demonstrate to stakeholders how Database Vault enables regulatory compliance while DBAs maintain their administrative capabilities, proving that your security model relies on technical enforcement, not trust alone 29 829 23 845 29 829 96 828 151 844 available_shared_title_scope shared_title_across_wms_records Dashboard metrics are title-level and shared by 2 current WMS records; they are not LiveLabs-ID-specific. - Run mission-critical OLTP and analytics workloads directly within Azure. 
- Integrate Oracle databases with Azure services

Using AIDP Workbench's visual agent flow canvas, you'll combine RAG over internal strategy documents with SQL tools querying box office, streaming, and marketing data — then deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint. No coding required. In this hands-on workshop, you'll design, configure, test, and deploy a Release & Performance Analyst Agent — an AI-powered assistant built on Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) that serves entertainment marketing, finance, and content strategy teams from a single, governed interface.
The entertainment industry generates data across dozens of disconnected systems — box office receipts, streaming viewership, media spend, and internal strategy documents — but the teams who need that data are all pulling from different sources with different definitions of success. This workshop demonstrates how AIDP unifies structured data and internal knowledge into an AI agent that any team can query in natural language.
The agent you'll build combines two capabilities: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal release playbooks, marketing measurement guidelines, and distribution rules; and SQL tools that execute parameterized queries against an Oracle AI Database containing box office, streaming, and marketing campaign data.
Lab 1 — Data Environment Setup (15 min): Explore the pre-configured standard catalog and managed volume in AIDP Workbench. Create a Knowledge Base that converts internal strategy documents into vector embeddings for semantic search. Verify the Oracle AI Database tables that contain box office, streaming, and marketing performance data.
Lab 2 — Agent Flow Setup (25 min): Create an AI Compute to host the agent. Build the agent flow on AIDP's visual canvas — configuring an agent node with a foundation model and detailed behavioral instructions, wiring up a RAG tool connected to the Knowledge Base, and adding seven SQL tools that cover box office performance, streaming health, campaign summaries, channel breakdowns, and reference lookups.
Lab 3 — Validate the Agent Flow (15 min): Test the agent in the Playground with real-world scenarios — multi-title box office comparisons (with typo handling), market-specific follow-ups that maintain conversational context, marketing ROI with channel breakdowns, cross-title streaming analysis, and custom tabular output on demand.
Lab 4 — Deploy the Agent Flow (5 min): Deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint on an AI Compute. Retrieve the endpoint URL and understand how external applications, dashboards, and integrations can consume the agent via REST API with OCI authentication. 14 984 6 989 14 984 available_shared_title_scope shared_title_across_wms_records Dashboard metrics are title-level and shared by 2 current WMS records; they are not LiveLabs-ID-specific. Healthcare organizations rely on multiple systems such as Electronic Medical Records (EMR), insurance platforms, and clinical applications to manage patient data. However, integrating these systems and accessing healthcare data in a standardized way remains a significant challenge.

Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) is a widely adopted standard that enables seamless exchange of healthcare information across systems. By leveraging FHIR APIs, organizations can efficiently retrieve and manage critical healthcare data such as patient records, appointments, medications, and practitioner details.

Customize AI Agents and Workflows with LLMs and OCI AI Agent Platform—Finance Edition

Unlock the power of OCI AI Agent Platform in this immersive LiveLab! Build a smart AI agent that helps compliance officers and risk managers review loan applications, monitor workloads, and check policy adherence—seamlessly accessing both your Oracle AI Database and lending policy documents using natural language.

If you’ve been curious how intelligent AI agents actually work behind the scenes, this hands-on workshop is your next step. You’ll build and customize a finance-focused AI agent using the OCI AI Agent Platform and large language models (LLMs) to help compliance officers and risk managers make smarter loan decisions. You will configure tools that allow the agent to query live data from Oracle AI Database and retrieve insights from policy manuals stored in Object Storage—combining structured and unstructured sources. You will learn how to connect these tools to an AI Agent, test multi-step reasoning with real compliance scenarios, and deliver policy-cited answers that explain the “why” behind each decision. Along the way, you’ll experiment with agent workflows, prompts, and configurations, and see how easily the OCI AI Agent Platform can bring context-aware intelligence to your enterprise use cases. By the end, you’ll have a fully functioning financial compliance AI agent—built, tested, and ready to adapt for your own organization’s workflows.

Learn to create database-powered agents with persistent memory, semantic search, and enterprise data access using Oracle Select AI Agent framework. Hands-on with SQL. Most AI systems can answer questions. AI agents are built to do work.

In this hands-on workshop, you will build AI agents for a financial services company called Seer Equity. Their current systems cannot answer simple questions like loan status or pending applications. Instead of returning results, they explain how to look things up. That breaks trust and frustrates clients.

You will build AI agents that connect directly to a loan database and return real answers. When asked about a loan, the agent queries data and responds with the current status, amount, and owner. You will see exactly what the agent did and why it did it.

During the workshop, you will:

Build AI agents that act on data instead of explaining steps

Store and recall client information across interactions

Use prior decisions to guide new ones

Apply company policies stored in the database

Record every action for audit and compliance

You will use Oracle Database and the Select AI Agent framework to define tools, agents, tasks, and teams using SQL. By the end, you will have a working loan processing system built around AI agents that behave consistently and can be trusted.

No machine learning background required. This lab covers installing the platform, configuring search targets using AI Vector Search, and embedding the search widget into web applications to deliver deterministic, data-driven outcomes without the risks and "guesswork" of generic chatbots. Enterprises increasingly demand natural-language interfaces, but traditional LLM-based "chatbots" often introduce unacceptable risks regarding accuracy, predictability, and data security. Oracle Trusted Answer Search addresses these challenges by providing a purpose-built "language-to-report" mapping system.
In this workshop, you will go hands-on with the primary components of the platform. You will start by deploying the core APEX-based administration and portal tools on the Oracle AI Database 26ai, leveraging its native AI Vector Search capabilities to match user queries to vetted business reports.
You will then step into the role of a Search Admin to curate the user experience. You will learn how to define Search Targets associated with specific match documents (JSON), ensuring that your application responds with deterministic actions—like opening a precise URL—rather than generated (and potentially hallucinatory) text. The lab also covers advanced configuration, such as parameter extraction, which allows your search interface to identify specific values like "checking account" or "last Monday" to automatically filter the reports presented to the user.
Finally, you will explore the developer experience by integrating the provided Javascript widget into a web application and the admin workflow for continuous improvement. You will learn how to use query history and user feedback (upvotes/downvotes) to refine search accuracy and use built-in regression analysis to safely manage changes to your search domain. You will publish an Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory agent, inspect the integration endpoint, understand the session-cookie requirement, bridge the private backend with OCI API Gateway, and wire Oracle APEX PL/SQL to start and continue agent conversations without manual cookie handling. This LiveLabs workshop walks learners through the complete end-to-end process of connecting Oracle AI Database Private Agent Factory (PAF) to Oracle APEX using OCI API Gateway, APEX Web Credentials, and PL/SQL. Learners begin by publishing a working agent in Agent Factory, capturing the integration endpoint, and understanding the two core challenges in the integration: the browser-based session cookie required by PAF and the private-network, self-signed SSL setup that prevents a straightforward direct call from APEX. The workshop then shows how OCI API Gateway can be configured as the bridge between APEX and the private backend, including the required login and agent routes and the SSL verification settings needed for this pattern to work.

After the gateway is in place, learners move into Oracle APEX and implement the full server-side integration flow. They create secure Web Credentials for storing login information, build PL/SQL logic to fetch a fresh agent_factory_session cookie automatically, initialize a room for the conversation, and send user messages to the published agent through the gateway. They also learn how to parse NDJSON responses returned by the service and return those responses cleanly back into the APEX application. By the end of the workshop, participants will have a practical, production-oriented blueprint for integrating Oracle Agent Factory with Oracle APEX without relying on manual cookie copy-paste steps, while also understanding the architectural decisions, security considerations, and operational flow behind the solution. Build an AI Interactive Report in Oracle APEX 12084 4406 APEX ankita.beri@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed apex Mapped From Current Wms 4406 12084 Workshop Published Public Completed APEX 6/23/2026 5/14/2026 Individual author Individual .5 551 307 551 1728 3646 3646 apex Mapped From Current Wms github_pages Local Git mirror repository-level proxy (high confidence) high Repository-level Git proxy 2026-03-12 2026-03-12 Update copyright current year Lucian Brinzei Confirmed From Current Or Stable Id History Publish Type is present in the reconciled WMS record. 4406 12084 Workshop Published Public Completed APEX 6/23/2026 5/14/2026 Individual author Individual .5 https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=4406 ankita.beri@oracle.com DB Product Management Configuring interactive reports traditionally requires users to manually define filters, sorting, pivots, aggregates, groupings, and column selections. APEX AI Interactive Reports simplifies this process by allowing users to ask questions in plain language, while APEX automatically translates the request into the appropriate report actions based on the user’s intent. Interactive Reports in Oracle APEX already give end users a rich set of capabilities, including filtering, sorting, control breaks, highlighting, aggregations, charts, groupings, and pivots. These features are powerful and well established, but configuring them traditionally requires moving through multiple menus, dialogs, and report settings. In practice, that means some capabilities are not used as often as they could be because they take time to discover and apply.

APEX AI Interactive Reports changes that experience. Instead of manually configuring a report, users can ask a question in plain language and let APEX translate that request into the right report actions. Based on the intent of the prompt, APEX can apply filters, sorting, pivots, aggregates, groupings, and column selections automatically. Each AI-generated configuration is shown as a visible chip, making the result transparent, reviewable, and easy to refine.

This workshop shows how to use that capability with SCM data. Using a Supply Chain Management application and a replenishment-focused view, you will configure AI support, create an Interactive Report on view named SCM_REPLENISHMENT_V, add report-level and column-level context, and use both Search with AI and the chat assistant to analyze replenishment activity in natural language. 551 193 307 173 551 193 1728 167 3646 148 3646 262 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Development Development Database - Oracle APEX, Developer - Low Code Application Dev., Business User, Low Code Developer

Build an AI Procurement Agent in Oracle APEX 12086 4407 APEX sahaana.manavalan@oracle.com Workshop Published Public Completed apex Mapped From Current Wms 4407 12086 Workshop Published Public Completed APEX 5/14/2026 5/14/2026 Individual author Individual 1137 595 1137 3345 6279 6279 apex Mapped From Current Wms github_pages Local Git mirror repository-level proxy (high confidence) high Repository-level Git proxy 2026-03-12 2026-03-12 Update copyright current year Lucian Brinzei Confirmed From Current Or Stable Id History Publish Type is present in the reconciled WMS record. 4407 12086 Workshop Published Public Completed APEX 5/14/2026 5/14/2026 Individual author Individual https://livelabs.oracle.com/ords/dbpm/r/livelabs/view-workshop?wid=4407 https://oracle-livelabs.github.io/apex/scm-ai-agent/workshops/tenancy/ sahaana.manavalan@oracle.com DB Product Management This workshop showcases how AI Agents in Oracle APEX streamline inventory and warehouse management through conversational automation. Users can identify stock shortages, evaluate supplier options, review delivery performance, and create purchase orders quickly without navigating multiple reports, improving supply chain efficiency and decision-making. Managing stock shortages and supplier decisions manually takes time that warehouse teams do not always have. When an item drops below its reorder point and the replenishment alert is already CRITICAL, a warehouse manager needs answers fast: which items are at risk, which suppliers can help, and who has the best delivery record.

AI Agents in Oracle APEX give your application the ability to reason through these questions and act on the answers. Instead of navigating multiple reports and forms, a user can open a chat panel and have a guided conversation. The agent understands who the user is, retrieves the right data, compares options, asks for confirmation, and raises a purchase order, all without leaving the application.

This workshop focuses on the inventory and warehouse management aspects of supply chain: identifying stock shortages, evaluating supplier options, and raising purchase orders through a conversational AI Agent.

In this hands-on workshop, you will build an AI Procurement Agent for the APEX Inventory and Warehouse Management application. You will define tools that allow warehouse managers to identify stock shortages, evaluate suppliers, and raise purchase orders, all from within a conversational chat interface in Oracle APEX.

You will define eight tools using the three tool types available in APEX AI Agents: Retrieve Data, Execute Server-side Code, and Execute Client-side Code. You will also learn when to use each one, all configured declaratively within Oracle APEX. 1137 148 595 118 1137 148 3345 111 6279 98 6279 171 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 Development Development Database - Oracle APEX, Developer - Low Code Application Dev., Business User, Low Code Developer

This expense agent use case demonstrates an intelligent, end-to-end automation flow that transforms raw expense receipts into validated expense records with minimal manual intervention. The Big Star Memory Agent demo shows how support AI evolves from chatbot replies to trusted, governed operations. Across 11 scenes, you see planning, memory, grounded policy decisions, approvals, and architecture in action. All powered by Oracle AI Database 26ai. LiveLabs LiveStacks are real-working demos!
The Big Star Memory Agent Demo is a business-first learning journey that shows how AI agents move from basic chatbot behavior to trusted, enterprise-ready operations. Through 11 scenes and a conclusion, user follow a realistic customer support case and see how planning, memory, grounded responses, governance, and human approval work together to improve service quality and operational control.

The demo starts by comparing a generic chatbot with a context-aware agent, then shows how planning and memory continuity reduce repeated customer effort and speed up resolution. It demonstrates why policy-sensitive decisions must be grounded in trusted data, how different memory types shape decision quality, and how governed memory writes and decision traces protect reliability. User then explore approval dashboards, lightweight access controls, and a complete architecture view that ties all layers together. 

A central takeaway is that successful AI-agent programs need more than model quality. They need a durable operational foundation where customer context, workflow state, controls, and auditability stay aligned. 
The demo uses Oracle AI Database 26ai as that converged foundation, highlighting how organizations can scale AI-agent workflows with stronger consistency, lower operational friction, and clearer accountability.

User can also download the whole demo and deploy it in their own environment. 2 1072 2 1072 21 1044 217 653 286 827 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy Rook-Ceph, a cloud-native storage orchestrator, on Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE). Using AIDP Workbench's visual agent flow canvas, you'll combine RAG over internal strategy documents with SQL tools querying box office, streaming, and marketing data — then deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint. No coding required. In this hands-on workshop, you'll design, configure, test, and deploy a Release & Performance Analyst Agent — an AI-powered assistant built on Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) that serves entertainment marketing, finance, and content strategy teams from a single, governed interface.
The entertainment industry generates data across dozens of disconnected systems — box office receipts, streaming viewership, media spend, and internal strategy documents — but the teams who need that data are all pulling from different sources with different definitions of success. This workshop demonstrates how AIDP unifies structured data and internal knowledge into an AI agent that any team can query in natural language.
The agent you'll build combines two capabilities: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal release playbooks, marketing measurement guidelines, and distribution rules; and SQL tools that execute parameterized queries against an Oracle AI Database containing box office, streaming, and marketing campaign data.
Lab 1 — Data Environment Setup (15 min): Explore the pre-configured standard catalog and managed volume in AIDP Workbench. Create a Knowledge Base that converts internal strategy documents into vector embeddings for semantic search. Verify the Oracle AI Database tables that contain box office, streaming, and marketing performance data.
Lab 2 — Agent Flow Setup (25 min): Create an AI Compute to host the agent. Build the agent flow on AIDP's visual canvas — configuring an agent node with a foundation model and detailed behavioral instructions, wiring up a RAG tool connected to the Knowledge Base, and adding seven SQL tools that cover box office performance, streaming health, campaign summaries, channel breakdowns, and reference lookups.
Lab 3 — Validate the Agent Flow (15 min): Test the agent in the Playground with real-world scenarios — multi-title box office comparisons (with typo handling), market-specific follow-ups that maintain conversational context, marketing ROI with channel breakdowns, cross-title streaming analysis, and custom tabular output on demand.
Lab 4 — Deploy the Agent Flow (5 min): Deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint on an AI Compute. Retrieve the endpoint URL and understand how external applications, dashboards, and integrations can consume the agent via REST API with OCI authentication. 2 1140 745 402 745 577 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. From freeform to pre-defined and cost tracking tags, to automated search and filter of resources across your account, to implementing programmatic solutions to enforce tag-based governance. Tagging plays a crucial role in organizing and managing cloud resources. A tag is essentially a key value pair that can be added to cloud resources to enhance visibility and control. In Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), tagging is built into the Identity and Access Management (IAM) service, enabling users to systematically categorize and manage resources. The use of tagging further allows for activities such as cost tracking, resource discovery and management, filtering, and logical organization.

Oracle Autonomous AI Database on Dedicated Exadata Infrastructure (Autonomous AI Database) generates two critical log streams: the alert log for database diagnostics and the unified audit trail for security and compliance. Run this hands-on workshop to learn how to use True Cache to improve scalability by offloading queries and reducing the number of requests and connections to the primary database. Why use True Cache?
True Cache can be used to scale a read-mostly application even without partitioning data. When primary database becomes the bottleneck , True Cache can be used to offload the primary and scale the workload. Also the data is always consistent and recent within a single query, this is important when there are joins across multiple rows.


This usage model of true cache through the JDBC requires minimal application change to use the functionality. Applications connect to only one service. Application uses setReadOnly(true) and setReadOnly(false) calls to mark some sections of code as "read only". If True Cache instances are configured, the JDBC driver will internally maintain, for each logical connection, 2 physical connections, one to a primary instance and one to an True Cache instance. The JDBC driver automatically sends SQL statements in "read-only" blocks to the True Cache instance.

What's in the workshop
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a Primary database configured with True Cache. The demo application is a Java program using the 23c JDBC driver. Its simulates a high number of transactions for the primary database and how off loading the read only queries to true cache helps in application performance.

It demonstrates:

How to set up True Cache.
Schema creation and initial data load to the primary database

True Cache can be used to scale a read-mostly application even without partitioning data. When primary database becomes the bottleneck , True Cache can be used to offload the primary and scale the workload. Also the data is always consistent and recent within a single query, this is important when there are joins across multiple rows.


This usage model of true cache through the JDBC requires minimal application change to use the functionality. Applications connect to only one service. Application uses setReadOnly(true) and setReadOnly(false) calls to mark some sections of code as "read only". If True Cache instances are configured, the JDBC driver will internally maintain, for each logical connection, 2 physical connections, one to a primary instance and one to an True Cache instance. The JDBC driver automatically sends SQL statements in "read-only" blocks to the True Cache instance.

What's in the workshop
This workshop is based on a compute instance (a demo application) connected to a Primary database configured with True Cache. The demo application is a Java program using the 23c JDBC driver. Its simulates a high number of transactions for the primary database and how off loading the read only queries to true cache helps in application performance.

It demonstrates:

How to set up True Cache.
Schema creation and initial data load to the primary database
The demo application shows the transactions running against the primary database and how switching to true cache helps in performance improvement .

Using AIDP Workbench's visual agent flow canvas, you'll combine RAG over internal strategy documents with SQL tools querying box office, streaming, and marketing data — then deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint. No coding required. In this hands-on workshop, you'll design, configure, test, and deploy a Release & Performance Analyst Agent — an AI-powered assistant built on Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) that serves entertainment marketing, finance, and content strategy teams from a single, governed interface.
The entertainment industry generates data across dozens of disconnected systems — box office receipts, streaming viewership, media spend, and internal strategy documents — but the teams who need that data are all pulling from different sources with different definitions of success. This workshop demonstrates how AIDP unifies structured data and internal knowledge into an AI agent that any team can query in natural language.
The agent you'll build combines two capabilities: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal release playbooks, marketing measurement guidelines, and distribution rules; and SQL tools that execute parameterized queries against an Oracle AI Database containing box office, streaming, and marketing campaign data.
Lab 1 — Data Environment Setup (15 min): Explore the pre-configured standard catalog and managed volume in AIDP Workbench. Create a Knowledge Base that converts internal strategy documents into vector embeddings for semantic search. Verify the Oracle AI Database tables that contain box office, streaming, and marketing performance data.
Lab 2 — Agent Flow Setup (25 min): Create an AI Compute to host the agent. Build the agent flow on AIDP's visual canvas — configuring an agent node with a foundation model and detailed behavioral instructions, wiring up a RAG tool connected to the Knowledge Base, and adding seven SQL tools that cover box office performance, streaming health, campaign summaries, channel breakdowns, and reference lookups.
Lab 3 — Validate the Agent Flow (15 min): Test the agent in the Playground with real-world scenarios — multi-title box office comparisons (with typo handling), market-specific follow-ups that maintain conversational context, marketing ROI with channel breakdowns, cross-title streaming analysis, and custom tabular output on demand.
Lab 4 — Deploy the Agent Flow (5 min): Deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint on an AI Compute. Retrieve the endpoint URL and understand how external applications, dashboards, and integrations can consume the agent via REST API with OCI authentication. 14 984 6 989 14 984 available_shared_title_scope shared_title_across_wms_records Dashboard metrics are title-level and shared by 2 current WMS records; they are not LiveLabs-ID-specific. Using AIDP Workbench's visual agent flow canvas, you'll combine RAG over internal strategy documents with SQL tools querying box office, streaming, and marketing data — then deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint. No coding required. In this hands-on workshop, you'll design, configure, test, and deploy a Release & Performance Analyst Agent — an AI-powered assistant built on Oracle AI Data Platform (AIDP) that serves entertainment marketing, finance, and content strategy teams from a single, governed interface.
The entertainment industry generates data across dozens of disconnected systems — box office receipts, streaming viewership, media spend, and internal strategy documents — but the teams who need that data are all pulling from different sources with different definitions of success. This workshop demonstrates how AIDP unifies structured data and internal knowledge into an AI agent that any team can query in natural language.
The agent you'll build combines two capabilities: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal release playbooks, marketing measurement guidelines, and distribution rules; and SQL tools that execute parameterized queries against an Oracle AI Database containing box office, streaming, and marketing campaign data.
Lab 1 — Data Environment Setup (15 min): Explore the pre-configured standard catalog and managed volume in AIDP Workbench. Create a Knowledge Base that converts internal strategy documents into vector embeddings for semantic search. Verify the Oracle AI Database tables that contain box office, streaming, and marketing performance data.
Lab 2 — Agent Flow Setup (25 min): Create an AI Compute to host the agent. Build the agent flow on AIDP's visual canvas — configuring an agent node with a foundation model and detailed behavioral instructions, wiring up a RAG tool connected to the Knowledge Base, and adding seven SQL tools that cover box office performance, streaming health, campaign summaries, channel breakdowns, and reference lookups.
Lab 3 — Validate the Agent Flow (15 min): Test the agent in the Playground with real-world scenarios — multi-title box office comparisons (with typo handling), market-specific follow-ups that maintain conversational context, marketing ROI with channel breakdowns, cross-title streaming analysis, and custom tabular output on demand.
Lab 4 — Deploy the Agent Flow (5 min): Deploy the agent to a production REST endpoint on an AI Compute. Retrieve the endpoint URL and understand how external applications, dashboards, and integrations can consume the agent via REST API with OCI authentication. 420 224 414 150 420 224 1193 205 1193 317 1193 502 available_unique_title_scope exact_unique_title Dashboard metrics matched one current WMS title. 1 AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Database - Data Warehouse/Lakehouse, Development - Analytics, Development - Database AI Services - AI/Machine Learning, Database - Data Warehouse/Lakehouse, Development - Analytics, Development - Database AI Services - AI Vector Search, Database - Oracle AI Database, Database Cloud Service - Autonomous AI Lakehouse Application Dev., Business Analyst, Data Scientist, Developer, Technology Manager

Enterprise AI agents become valuable when they can operate across real business systems, not just answer questions. In this hands-on lab, participants will build a private Purchase Order agent that connects to Fusion ERP, Oracle Database, and representative customer applications to help users inspect PO status, query supplier and order data, reason across systems, and trigger governed business workflows.
The lab will introduce a repeatable Private Agent Factory pattern that business IT teams can use to design, build, secure, observe, and scale enterprise agents. In this hands-on workshop, participants will use prompts to integrate OCI AI models into applications and leverage HeatWave’s native AI and vector capabilities to create intelligent, scalable, and data-driven shopping experiences. Discover how to build intelligent, AI-powered applications using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI Services, Visual Studio Code, and MySQL HeatWave. In this hands-on workshop, participants will develop a modern eCommerce web application enhanced with generative AI capabilities, demonstrating how AI can transform customer experiences and application workflows.

The workshop introduces developers to prompt-driven application development using enterprise-grade OCI AI models directly from Visual Studio Code. Participants will learn how to integrate OCI Generative AI APIs into web applications, design effective prompts, and build interactive AI-powered features such as product recommendations, conversational shopping assistants, content generation, product search, and personalized user experiences.

In addition to OCI Generative AI Services, the workshop highlights the power of MySQL HeatWave and its native AI capabilities, including vector storage, semantic search and AI-driven data processing. Attendees will gain practical experience combining structured application data with AI-enhanced search and recommendation workflows to build scalable, intelligent applications.

Throughout the session, participants will:

* Set up and configure OCI Generative AI Services
* Use Visual Studio Code for AI-assisted development workflows
* Integrate prompts and AI model inference into web applications
* Connect applications with MySQL HeatWave
* Explore HeatWave’s native AI and vector capabilities
* Build and test AI-powered eCommerce features end-to-end

An employee record may have related paystubs, contact details, goals, documents, orders, attachments, or line items. You do not want to maintain separate user-specific predicates for every child table.

Participants must use their own OCI tenancy with the required IAM permissions, service limits, and VLAN support. This workshop guides participants through building and validating a complete Oracle Linux Virtualization Manager (OLVM) environment on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using their own OCI tenancy.

Participants are responsible for bringing access to an OCI tenancy and target compartment where they have permission to create compute, networking, storage, public IP, VLAN, and NAT Gateway resources. records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Build AI applications with the Oracle Autonomous AI Vector Database Python SDK for vector search, embeddings, semantic retrieval, and Oracle AI Agent Memory.

Autonomous AI Vector Database is a fully managed vector database service that enables developers to quickly build AI-powered applications using Python, REST APIs, and SQL. Built on Oracle Autonomous Database, it combines a simple developer experience with enterprise capabilities such as automated provisioning, scaling, backups, and security.
In this LiveLab, you'll provision an Autonomous AI Vector Database, connect using the Oracle Python SDK, create a vector table, load sample data, and automatically generate vector embeddings. You'll then perform semantic searches using natural language and see how vector search can be combined with metadata filtering to deliver more relevant results.
You'll also integrate Oracle Agent Memory to add conversational memory to your application, enabling it to retain context across interactions and deliver more personalized responses.
By the end of the lab, you'll understand the core workflow for building AI-powered search applications with Autonomous AI Vector Database and see how semantic search and conversational memory work together to create richer AI experiences.

records.title: Build a Medallion Data Pipeline with Oracle AI Lakehouse
records.rawTitle: Build a Medallion Data Pipeline with Oracle AI Lakehouse
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Build a governed medallion pipeline with Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse, Apache Iceberg, Data Transforms, AI Catalog, and Select AI.

In this hands-on lab, you will build an end-to-end medallion pipeline using PeakGear retail data. You will load raw data into open Apache Iceberg Bronze tables, cleanse and enrich it in Silver, and use Oracle AI Data Catalog to discover an additional governed inventory dataset. You will then combine the Silver datasets to answer a replenishment question and publish a trusted native Oracle Gold data product for business consumption.

Finally, you will use Select AI natural-language queries to analyze curated Gold data and generate sales, margin, and inventory insights. The lab demonstrates a practical, open, multi-cloud-ready architecture for modernizing data pipelines while making governed data easier for data engineers, analysts, business users, and AI agents to discover and use.

records.title: Build Connected Hospitality Solutions with Oracle AI Database
records.rawTitle: Build Connected Hospitality Solutions with Oracle AI Database
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Build a workshop around a hospitality LiveStack to demonstrate how Oracle AI Database unifies guest profiles, reservations, properties, stays, loyalty activity, service interactions, spatial property data, vector search, predictive analytics, and AI-assisted data access in one governed data foundation.

This workshop teaches learners how a hospitality organization can use Oracle AI Database as a single converged data platform for guest experience, property operations, reservations, loyalty, service delivery, and AI-driven analytics.

Using a hospitality LiveStack, learners explore a connected hospitality application backed by relational tables, JSON Relational Duality Views, property graphs, spatial data, vector embeddings, in-database machine learning, Virtual Private Database policies, natural-language SQL with Select AI, and agent-style workflows with Select AI Agents.

The workshop demonstrates how governed hospitality data; including guest profiles, reservations, stays, properties, amenities, loyalty relationships, and service interactions; can be securely served to dashboards, applications, APIs, analysts, property teams, and AI experiences without copying sensitive guest or operational data into separate specialized systems.

records.title: Oracle Deep Data Security and Microsoft Entra ID authentication
records.rawTitle: Oracle Deep Data Security and Microsoft Entra ID authentication
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: This lab shows how to integrate Microsoft Entra ID with Oracle AI Database 26ai and apply Deep Data Security so the database enforces per-user access based on identity. Users like Marvin and Emma authenticate via Entra ID and see different results from the same query.

This lab walks you through configuring Microsoft Entra ID authentication for Oracle AI Database 26ai and then layering Oracle Deep Data Security — end users, data roles, and data grants — so the database enforces per-user access based on Entra ID app role assignments. By the end, Marvin (a manager) and Emma (an employee) will authenticate with Entra ID and see completely different data from the same SQL query, enforced by the database kernel.

details:

records.rawTitle: No More NULL Answers: Build Smarter Support with PostgreSQL and OCI AI
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Build an support agent using OCI Database with PostgreSQL and OCI Enterprise AI. Retrieve relevant business data, understand customer questions, and deliver grounded responses—improving support quality and resolution speed with a repeatable AI application pattern.

Your business data becomes more valuable when AI can understand and act on it. In this hands-on lab, you’ll connect OCI Database with PostgreSQL to a large language model using OCI Enterprise AI and build a customer support agent that can retrieve relevant business data, understand customer questions, and generate grounded responses. You’ll combine enterprise data with AI to create a practical workflow that improves response quality and helps support teams resolve requests faster. Leave with a working customer support agent and a repeatable pattern for building AI applications grounded in PostgreSQL data on OCI.

Learn how to build enterprise-ready AI applications on OCI PostgreSQL using vector search, PostgreSQL full-text search, pgvector-powered RAG, and OCI Enterprise AI services.

records.rawTitle: One Restaurant, Every Model: From Document Pain to Converged Resolution
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: One restaurant chain, every data model. Ship a fully embedded menu through the MongoDB API, feel that bet invert when corporate changes one price, then model it properly and get the document back as a JSON Relational Duality View. Finish with a property graph and AI Vector Search over the same rows - one database, one transaction, one optimizer.

AI applications need trusted operational data across documents, relational tables, graph relationships and vector search - without copies, pipelines, or consistency gaps. This hands-on workshop makes that concrete on one small dataset: a five-location restaurant chain, modelled every way the database can model it, with the same rows underneath the whole time.

You start where most teams start. Using the Oracle Database API for MongoDB and an unmodified mongosh, you seed a fully embedded menu document per location - no joins, no ORM, the shape your application wants. Then corporate raises one price chain-wide, and you watch the embedded bet invert on every dial at once: a one-number change becomes a fleet-wide document rewrite, a simple analytics question becomes a fan-out pipeline, and one drifted copy quietly stops being true without raising an error.

From there you fix the physics rather than the query. The collection your Mongo shell wrote is already a JSON Collection Table, so you shred it in place into a canonical relational schema - a chain catalog plus the junction that records which location offers which item, at what local price. Corporate's price becomes one row, at five locations or seven thousand five hundred. Then a JSON Relational Duality View hands the document ergonomics back, assembled live from those rows, with per-field write governance the engine enforces against every API: the same ORA-02290 through mongosh that SQL raises, because there is one rulebook rather than a validation layer per surface.

The last third turns the same data into shapes a document store cannot reach. Orders stay native JSON, flattened into a SQL/PGQ property graph that answers "do you want fries with that" as a two-hop MATCH. AI Vector Search embeds the menu in place with an ONNX model running inside the database, so a brand-new dish is findable by meaning on the same commit that created it - no sync pipeline, no staleness window. The finale is one statement that walks the graph, joins the relational truth and ranks by vector distance, planned as one tree by one optimizer.

Every observable in the workshop is a count or a value you can verify yourself, and every code block ships executed against a live 26ai database rather than merely proofread.

records.title: Hybrid Vector Search and Vector Indexes on Iceberg for next-gen AI apps
records.rawTitle: Hybrid Vector Search and Vector Indexes on Iceberg for next-gen AI apps
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Build AI applications that deliver more accurate and relevant results across all types of data using advanced vector techniques such as hybrid vector search indexes and vector indexes on iceberg tables.

Build AI applications that deliver more accurate and relevant results across all types of data using advanced vector techniques such as hybrid vector search indexes and vector indexes on iceberg tables. In this hands-on lab, you'll learn how to combine semantic vector search with deterministic keyword search to improve retrieval quality for RAG applications, AI agents, and enterprise search and be able to easily run semantic searches against high volume iceberg data in object store.  

You'll create a hybrid index, a vector index on iceberg, execute hybrid queries, and compare the results against traditional vector-only and keyword-only search. Along the way, you'll learn how Hybrid Vector Search improves recall and precision by combining semantic similarity with exact keyword matching—making it easier to retrieve documents containing required entities such as names, products, or locations while still capturing semantic meaning. 

Using Oracle Database, you'll build and optimize hybrid retrieval pipelines through a unified indexing and query interface, leaving with practical techniques for developing production-ready AI applications with more accurate and trustworthy search results.

records.title: Build Trusted Enterprise RAG Applications with Oracle AI Vector Search
records.rawTitle: Build Trusted Enterprise RAG Applications with Oracle AI Vector Search
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Build a real-world RAG pipeline using Oracle AI Vector Search in Oracle AI Database 26ai, SQL, and Private AI Services Container.

Large language models are powerful, but they can't answer questions about your organization's enterprise data without relevant context. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Oracle AI Vector Search addresses this challenge by retrieving the most relevant information from your enterprise data and grounding LLM responses with that context. 
In this lab, you'll build a real-world RAG pipeline using Oracle AI Vector Search in Oracle AI Database 26ai, SQL, and Private AI Services Container. You'll learn how unstructured documents are transformed into vector embeddings, perform semantic similarity searches over enterprise data, and use the retrieved context to generate accurate, context-aware natural language responses. 
To conclude the session, you'll explore a pre-built Oracle APEX chatbot that uses the same SQL-based retrieval pipeline you built, demonstrating how Oracle AI Vector Search can be integrated into enterprise applications to deliver secure, intelligent conversational experiences.

records.title: Working with Gateways in OCI Internet of Things (IoT) Platform
records.rawTitle: Working with Gateways in OCI Internet of Things (IoT) Platform
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Learn how OCI IoT Platform gateways connect and manage devices that cannot connect directly to OCI. Create a gateway, route incoming telemetry to indirectly connected water-pump digital twins, and verify their normalized state.

Learn how to use OCI Internet of Things (IoT) Platform gateways to connect devices that cannot communicate directly with OCI. You create a gateway digital twin, configure its status model and routing adapter, and register indirectly connected water-pump twins that use both standard and flat-telemetry adapters. You then publish telemetry through the gateway’s single MQTT connection and verify that OCI routes, normalizes, and updates each target twin correctly.
Completing the lab gives you a practical pattern for bringing existing field equipment, legacy devices, and constrained networks into an IoT solution without requiring direct cloud connectivity for every device. You will understand how gateways reduce connection-management overhead, centralize authentication, and support consistent digital-twin state across a distributed device fleet.

records.title: Build AI Agents on Enterprise Data with Oracle AI Lakehouse
records.rawTitle: Build AI Agents on Enterprise Data with Oracle AI Lakehouse
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Connect Databricks Unity/Iceberg and an existing Oracle operations database to Oracle AI Lakehouse. Use Data Studio AI Enrichment and Codex through MCP to turn a vague product-interest question into governed Analytic Views and an explainable cross-source recommendation.

PeakGear has product and digital-interaction data in Databricks Unity Catalog and returns data in an existing Oracle operations database. Participants configure a bounded PEAKGEAR_USER environment, connect both sources to Oracle AI Lakehouse, and connect Codex Desktop through the Oracle Data Studio MCP Server.

They first ask a raw product-interest question and observe that an assistant should not invent a ranking when business semantics are undefined. In Oracle Data Studio, they review and save business meaning with AI Enrichment. For a cross-source question, they identify where annotations and tags are insufficient, then use Codex through MCP to create and validate governed Analytic Views with common time, product, category, aggregation, and drill-down semantics.

The final answer ranks product categories by current interest with returned-units context and provides supporting product-level evidence. The lab demonstrates Oracle AI Lakehouse as a governed decision layer across live Oracle and Databricks data, with Data Studio as the primary interface and Codex Desktop as the AI client.

records.title: Get Started with OCI Internet of Things (IoT) Platform
records.rawTitle: Get Started with OCI Internet of Things (IoT) Platform
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: Learn how to use OCI IoT Platform digital twins to model, connect, and monitor physical devices. Create an asset hierarchy, build reusable equipment and component models, configure adapters, create twin instances, send telemetry through HTTP, and verify data in the OCI CLI and Console.

Organizations across manufacturing, energy, utilities, transportation, logistics, retail, healthcare, and smart buildings depend on physical assets that must operate reliably. Pumps, motors, compressors, refrigeration units, conveyors, generators, vehicles, and other equipment produce valuable operational data, but that data often remains isolated in vendor systems or arrives in inconsistent formats.
This hands-on workshop introduces OCI Internet of Things Platform and its digital twin capabilities through a practical equipment-monitoring scenario that applies across industries. You will learn how to represent physical assets and their relationships in a shared digital model, connect telemetry from different sources, and use incoming data to understand equipment condition and performance.
You begin by setting up the OCI resources needed for the workshop and reviewing a realistic operational use case. The scenario uses a hierarchy of sites, operational areas, and equipment, but the same approach can represent a factory with production lines, a utility network with pumping stations, a fleet with vehicles, a hospital with critical systems, or a building portfolio with HVAC equipment.
Next, you create a digital representation of the asset environment. You model a parent facility and define related operating areas without requiring each entity to connect directly to a device. This captures the business and physical context around connected equipment. For example, a pump can belong to a production line, a compressor can serve a refrigeration zone, or a vehicle can operate within a fleet and depot structure.
You then build reusable digital twin models for equipment and its components. The workshop uses a water-pump model that includes a motor component, demonstrating how to compose a complete asset from smaller reusable models. You define telemetry properties such as flow rate, pressure, motor temperature, vibration, and power consumption. These properties use quantitative data types, validation rules, and history so teams can capture measurements consistently, reject invalid values, and review changes over time.
The workshop also covers digital twin adapters. Real devices and control systems rarely publish telemetry in the same structure, even when they report the same measurement. You create a default adapter and a flat telemetry adapter to map different payload formats to the shared digital twin model. This pattern helps organizations normalize telemetry from equipment supplied by different vendors, deployed at different sites, or connected through different gateways.
After defining the models and adapters, you create digital twin instances for individual assets and establish relationships between facilities, operating areas, equipment, and components. In the final lab, you send telemetry through HTTP, verify data ingestion with the OCI CLI, and view asset data in the OCI Console.
By the end of the workshop, you will understand how OCI IoT Platform digital twins support condition monitoring, maintenance planning, performance comparison, issue investigation, and data-driven asset management.

Ensure continuous protection of sensitive data, detect risks early, enforce access controls, and help organizations stay compliant and secure against evolving threats. In the era of digital transformation and heightened regulatory expectations, data security is no longer optional—it is a vital necessity. Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF) is a robust solution that empowers organizations to safeguard their most valuable digital assets from both internal and external threats. With AVDF, your databases are protected through advanced auditing, real-time monitoring, and proactive defense mechanisms, all managed from a unified, streamlined interface.

Why Attend this LiveLab?

Do you worry about meeting complex compliance mandates such as PCI DSS, SOX, or GDPR? Are you tasked with defending your organization against sophisticated cyber threats while enabling business agility? This hands-on LiveLab is the perfect environment for data professionals, security administrators, and auditors to experience first-hand how AVDF helps organizations secure sensitive information, streamline compliance, and respond rapidly to suspicious activity—before damage is done. 

What Problem Does AVDF Solve?

Modern database environments are highly dynamic and increasingly targeted by cyber attackers. Insiders with privileged access often represent the greatest risk, whether through error or deliberate misuse. Traditional logging and monitoring solutions frequently fall short—missing subtle policy violations or producing overwhelming volumes of raw data that are hard to interpret and act upon. Furthermore, regulatory auditors demand immediate, centralized, and immutable proof of how sensitive data is accessed and who is responsible. 

AVDF bridges these gaps by:

 - Centralizing and automating the collection, consolidation, and analysis of audit data from Oracle and non-Oracle databases.
    - Delivering real-time monitoring and alerts to detect unusual or unauthorized SQL activity—down to the individual statement.
    - Enforcing fine-grained controls at the network edge with the Database Firewall, blocking unwanted or suspicious commands before they can cause harm.
    - Offering a rich suite of compliance-ready reports and dashboards for continuous assurance.
     
What You’ll Experience in this LiveLab

In this interactive session, you'll step into the shoes of a security analyst or compliance officer as you: 

    - Deploy and configure AVDF for both Oracle and non-Oracle database environments
    - Set up real-time auditing policies and analyze collected data through intuitive dashboards
    - Use the Database Firewall to enforce strong security controls, detect policy violations, and block malicious SQL traffic
    - Respond to simulated threats, generate compliance reports, and implement best practices for the separation of duties
     
With guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain practical skills you can immediately apply to your organization’s security and compliance strategy. No prior AVDF experience is required—just a willingness to learn and a desire to witness the power of Oracle’s database security solutions. 

Who Should Attend?

    - Database Administrators
    - Security Engineers
    - Auditors and Compliance Officers
    - IT Managers and Risk Professionals
     
Whether you are wrestling with stricter compliance mandates, tightening your security posture, or just curious about next-generation database protection, this LiveLab will inspire you to rethink what’s possible with AVDF.

With AVDF, your databases are protected through advanced auditing, real-time monitoring, and proactive defense mechanisms, all managed from a unified, streamlined interface.

Why Attend this LiveLab?

Do you worry about meeting complex compliance mandates such as PCI DSS, SOX, or GDPR? Are you tasked with defending your organization against sophisticated cyber threats while enabling business agility? This hands-on LiveLab is the perfect environment for data professionals, security administrators, and auditors to experience first-hand how AVDF helps organizations secure sensitive information, streamline compliance, and respond rapidly to suspicious activity—before damage is done. 

What Problem Does AVDF Solve?

Modern database environments are highly dynamic and increasingly targeted by cyber attackers. Insiders with privileged access often represent the greatest risk, whether through error or deliberate misuse. Traditional logging and monitoring solutions frequently fall short—missing subtle policy violations or producing overwhelming volumes of raw data that are hard to interpret and act upon. Furthermore, regulatory auditors demand immediate, centralized, and immutable proof of how sensitive data is accessed and who is responsible. 

AVDF bridges these gaps by:

 - Centralizing and automating the collection, consolidation, and analysis of audit data from Oracle and non-Oracle databases.
    - Delivering real-time monitoring and alerts to detect unusual or unauthorized SQL activity—down to the individual statement.
    - Enforcing fine-grained controls at the network edge with the Database Firewall, blocking unwanted or suspicious commands before they can cause harm.
    - Offering a rich suite of compliance-ready reports and dashboards for continuous assurance.
     
What You’ll Experience in this LiveLab

In this interactive session, you'll step into the shoes of a security analyst or compliance officer as you: 

    - Deploy and configure AVDF for both Oracle and non-Oracle database environments
    - Set up real-time auditing policies and analyze collected data through intuitive dashboards
    - Use the Database Firewall to enforce strong security controls, detect policy violations, and block malicious SQL traffic
    - Respond to simulated threats, generate compliance reports, and implement best practices for the separation of duties
     
With guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain practical skills you can immediately apply to your organization’s security and compliance strategy. No prior AVDF experience is required—just a willingness to learn and a desire to witness the power of Oracle’s database security solutions. 

Who Should Attend?

    - Database Administrators
    - Security Engineers
    - Auditors and Compliance Officers
    - IT Managers and Risk Professionals
     
Whether you are wrestling with stricter compliance mandates, tightening your security posture, or just curious about next-generation database protection, this LiveLab will inspire you to rethink what’s possible with AVDF. 

Take the next step in your data security journey—join us for the AVDF LiveLab and unlock the tools to secure your enterprise database estates, meet compliance demands with confidence, and fend off the threats of tomorrow. Your path to resilient database defense starts here.

details: Build a retail RAG application using Oracle Autonomous AI Database, Oracle AI Vector Search, Azure OpenAI, and Azure Machine Learning. Load a fashion product catalog, generate embeddings, perform semantic search, and test natural-language shopping questions.

Learners prepare and load a fashion product catalog, generate product-title embeddings with Azure OpenAI, and use Oracle AI Vector Search to find products by meaning rather than keywords. The workshop supports both Oracle-provided Azure Event Accounts and regular Azure accounts.

records.rawTitle: Deploy a healthcare integration engine on OCI
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: This workshop walks through the steps of creating necessary OCI resources and deploying a popular open-source healthcare integration engine.

Healthcare interoperability has evolved far beyond connecting systems within a single hospital. While interface engines continue to route HL7 messages between electronic health records (EHRs), laboratories, pharmacies, and imaging systems, today's healthcare organizations face a much broader challenge. They must deliver a seamless digital experience across multiple hospitals and clinics, support care coordination, expose FHIR APIs, integrate AI into clinical workflows, and securely exchange data with partners, payers, and public health agencies all while continuing to rely on mission-critical on-premises clinical systems that remain essential to patient care.

Replacing these existing systems is rarely practical. Instead, healthcare organizations are extending their interoperability investments by adopting a hybrid architecture that combines proven on-premises solutions with cloud-native services. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) provides a secure, scalable, and high-performance platform for building this next generation of healthcare integration.

In this Oracle LiveLabs workshop, you will provision the minimum OCI infrastructure required to host an integration engine and then deploy the open-source edition of Mirth Connect on OCI. Along the way, you'll learn how to create the essential OCI resources, configure the environment, and prepare a cloud-based interoperability platform that can serve as the foundation for modern healthcare integration solutions.

Oracle AI Database, not application code or an AI prompt, decides which rows and columns each user can see. You then test the same boundary with OCI Generative AI and with data outside the database. AI agents are creating new paths to enterprise data. records.title: LiveStack LiveLab Workshop - Build Higher Education Student Success Intelligence with Oracle AI Database 26ai
records.rawTitle: LiveStack LiveLab Workshop - Build Higher Education Student Success Intelligence with Oracle AI Database 26ai
records.source: 28 September 2026 WMS, dashboard views, and WMS tag reports; GitHub repository/update evidence retained from 14-15 August 2026
details: In this hands-on workshop, you will inspect the database objects behind the Higher Education LiveStack application and complete interactive SQL investigations using relational tables, JSON Relational Duality views, AI Vector Search, Property Graph, spatial data, and Oracle Machine Learning.

In this hands-on workshop, you will explore the database foundation behind the Seer Higher Education LiveStack.
Using Oracle Database Actions SQL Worksheet, you will inspect the objects and queries that power the student-success application experience, including the command center, student intent and support signals, advisor and program relationships, campus service coverage, unified request documents, and predictive student-success analytics.
The workshop shows how Oracle AI Database 26ai can keep student-success evidence close to the work. You will use relational SQL, JSON Relational Duality, AI Vector Search, Property Graph, Oracle Spatial, and Oracle Machine Learning to trace student-support decisions back to governed database evidence.
You will also complete short interactive tasks: change a business question, compare the resulting evidence, create and update a student request through JSON, and make a bounded recommendation for human review.
By the end, you will see how one connected data foundation can help higher-education teams observe demand, understand student signals, match needs to services, assess relationship and location context, manage requests, score demand, and prioritize human review.

details: Learn how to use keyword and semantic search on JSON collections with Oracle AI Database API for MongoDB.

Learn how to add keyword and semantic search to JSON movie data with Oracle Database API for MongoDB. During this workshop, you use SQL and mongosh with a MOVIES collection. You load an in-database ONNX model, generate summary embeddings, and create text and vector indexes. You then compare keyword, fuzzy, semantic, filtered, and combined searches.

The workshop follows an incremental path. You first access either a LiveLabs Sandbox or your OCI tenancy and connect through SQL and the MongoDB API. You then prepare the movie data and create the search indexes. Finally, you search movie summaries by meaning and combine keyword and vector results.

details: DB Security - Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF)

Monitor and safeguard databases with real-time activity tracking, advanced threat detection, and Database Security Posture Management (DSPM). Ensure continuous protection of sensitive data, detect risks early, enforce access controls, and help organizations stay compliant and secure against evolving threats.

In the era of digital transformation and heightened regulatory expectations, data security is no longer optional—it is a vital necessity. Oracle Audit Vault and Database Firewall (AVDF) is a robust solution that empowers organizations to safeguard their most valuable digital assets from both internal and external threats. With AVDF, your databases are protected through advanced auditing, real-time monitoring, and proactive defense mechanisms, all managed from a unified, streamlined interface.

Why Attend this LiveLab?

Do you worry about meeting complex compliance mandates such as PCI DSS, SOX, or GDPR? Are you tasked with defending your organization against sophisticated cyber threats while enabling business agility? This hands-on LiveLab is the perfect environment for data professionals, security administrators, and auditors to experience first-hand how AVDF helps organizations secure sensitive information, streamline compliance, and respond rapidly to suspicious activity—before damage is done. 

What Problem Does AVDF Solve?

Modern database environments are highly dynamic and increasingly targeted by cyber attackers. Insiders with privileged access often represent the greatest risk, whether through error or deliberate misuse. Traditional logging and monitoring solutions frequently fall short—missing subtle policy violations or producing overwhelming volumes of raw data that are hard to interpret and act upon. Furthermore, regulatory auditors demand immediate, centralized, and immutable proof of how sensitive data is accessed and who is responsible. 

AVDF bridges these gaps by:

 - Centralizing and automating the collection, consolidation, and analysis of audit data from Oracle and non-Oracle databases.
    - Delivering real-time monitoring and alerts to detect unusual or unauthorized SQL activity—down to the individual statement.
    - Enforcing fine-grained controls at the network edge with the Database Firewall, blocking unwanted or suspicious commands before they can cause harm.
    - Offering a rich suite of compliance-ready reports and dashboards for continuous assurance.
     
What You’ll Experience in this LiveLab

In this interactive session, you'll step into the shoes of a security analyst or compliance officer as you: 

    - Deploy and configure AVDF for both Oracle and non-Oracle database environments
    - Set up real-time auditing policies and analyze collected data through intuitive dashboards
    - Use the Database Firewall to enforce strong security controls, detect policy violations, and block malicious SQL traffic
    - Respond to simulated threats, generate compliance reports, and implement best practices for the separation of duties
     
With guided exercises and real-world scenarios, you’ll gain practical skills you can immediately apply to your organization’s security and compliance strategy. No prior AVDF experience is required—just a willingness to learn and a desire to witness the power of Oracle’s database security solutions. 

Who Should Attend?

    - Database Administrators
    - Security Engineers
    - Auditors and Compliance Officers
    - IT Managers and Risk Professionals
     
Whether you are wrestling with stricter compliance mandates, tightening your security posture, or just curious about next-generation database protection, this LiveLab will inspire you to rethink what’s possible with AVDF. 

Take the next step in your data security journey—join us for the AVDF LiveLab and unlock the tools to secure your enterprise database estates, meet compliance demands with confidence, and fend off the threats of tomorrow. Your path to resilient database defense starts here.
